## Development setup

Use Python 3.12 or newer and Poetry 2.4.x or newer within Poetry 2.x. From the
checkout, select your installed interpreter and install the locked development tools:

```sh
poetry env use python3.12
poetry install --with dev
poetry run obforce --help
poetry run python -m obforce --version
```

The static version lives in `pyproject.toml`; CLI version reporting reads installed
distribution metadata. Commit `poetry.lock` with approved dependency changes. Use
`poetry add` or `poetry update`; never hand-edit the lockfile or add a parallel
runtime requirements file. Runtime dependencies are Click, Jinja2 (candidate
templates/sandbox), and `defusedxml` for explicit offline XML DTD/entity/external-
reference refusal. Thread 08 adds `ruamel-yaml >=0.19.1,<0.20.0` (locked 0.19.1)
for bounded pure round-trip parsing and source spans; no optional C extension.
Candidate serialization continues to use a flat YAML-compatible JSON subset. Development
tools are pytest, pytest-cov, Ruff, Bandit, and Twine.

## Checks

```sh
poetry check --lock --strict
poetry run ruff check .
poetry run ruff format --check .
poetry run pytest -q -ra
poetry run pytest --cov=obforce --cov-report=term-missing
poetry run bandit -r src/obforce
git diff --check
```

CI first collects tests, then runs coverage through `dev/run_pytest.py` with
exclusive external logs, 2 MiB raw/console budgets, 4 KiB diagnostic lines and
5-minute collection / 45-minute test deadlines. Overflow is a failed incomplete
run, never a truncated pass. Collection rejects node IDs over 512 UTF-8 bytes;
use short descriptive IDs for large parameter values without shrinking fixtures.
CI prints bounded case IDs and the slowest 25 setup/call/teardown durations; a
timeout also exposes any bounded unfinished child line without implying a result.
Default pytest diagnostics use short tracebacks, omit captured-output dumps and
stop after five failure reports. Matrix fail-fast, workflow concurrency and outer
step/job deadlines limit redundant work. Cancelled/unexecuted cells remain gaps.
See [exact budgets and reproduction](docs/QUALIFICATION.md#bounded-ci-test-execution).

Tests are deterministic and offline, using temporary directories and synthetic
inputs. They never discover Salesforce authentication or use a real vault. The
entry-point integration tests block Python socket operations and remove external
tools from `PATH`. Dependency installation can require network access; installed
help/version operation does not. Do not install or invoke Salesforce CLI or
Obsidian for foundation tests.

Poetry's editable install generates an extensionless Python console script and,
on Windows, a `.cmd` wrapper. Integration tests invoke that installed Python
script through the active interpreter on Windows, with the same invocation
tested on other platforms. They fail if the script is missing. The separate
artifact checker directly runs pip-installed console executables (`obforce.exe`
on Windows) from clean wheel/sdist environments; neither check substitutes the
module entry point for the console script or skips Windows coverage.

Ruff targets Python 3.12, 130 columns, single-quoted ordinary strings,
triple-double-quoted docstrings, spaces, and LF. Use type hints at boundaries and
the Python headers in AGENTS.md, with the actual generating model and local date.

CI prepares a fresh directory under `runner.temp` after Python setup, exporting
`TMPDIR`, `TEMP` and `TMP` before Poetry installation. Subsequent test fixtures,
build setup and independent installed probes use that root rather than the busy
system-wide temporary directory. Full ancestor metadata checks intentionally
refuse changes during observation; unrelated entries in a shared ancestor can
therefore block an otherwise clean synthetic plan. Tests must run under a
quiescent temporary ancestry. This environment isolation does not change the
production read contract, add retries, skip guards or qualify hostile races.

The repository `.gitattributes` keeps text checkouts LF on Windows as well as
POSIX hosts, retaining automatic binary detection. Each CI environment-selection,
installation, and validation command runs in its own step so a later successful
native command cannot mask an earlier failure in PowerShell. A green job summary
is insufficient when command logs show a failed check. The Windows formatter
correction is delivered and verified; see the roadmap's
[Thread 02 acceptance record](dev/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md#thread-02-acceptance-and-closure--19-october-2026)
for the exact commit and hosted evidence.

SECURITY.md.utf8:
# Security and privacy

Obforce is under development. No stable release or supported-version security
maintenance window has been established. The current foundation provides local
help/version reporting; Salesforce collection and vault mutation are planned.

Report suspected vulnerabilities through GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting
in this repository's Security tab if enabled, or an established private maintainer
contact. If neither is available, request a private channel without posting
sensitive details in a public issue. Do not assume a response-time commitment.

Never post credentials, tokens, authentication URLs, real org metadata, audit
identities, internal endpoints, vault content, state, or recovery files. Use
fictional minimal reproductions and placeholder paths. Removing an org name alone
does not sanitize metadata or human-authored documentation.

Normal generation is intended to remain local, reuse explicitly selected existing
Salesforce CLI authentication, and avoid telemetry, AI services, hosted storage,
and credential collection. These are design constraints, not claims that the
future source/writer safety boundaries are implemented. Real org or vault tests
require separate explicit authorization. Keep private material in ignored
`local/` and use independent vault backups when those workflows become available.

# Configuration contract

Thread 02 implements an internal, read-only config loader and source selection.
Public `init`, initial `build` and `recover` are implemented in Thread 12;
Thread 13 adds [managed-vault sync](REFRESH.md) with private persistent evidence.
The approved [design](../dev/THREAD_13_PERSISTENT_EVIDENCE_DESIGN.md) records the
state-version split, live scope declarations and per-invocation attestation.
See the public command contract below and fictional
[quickstart](QUICKSTART.md). The following config also documents internal validation.
Internal Python interfaces are versioned implementation details, not a stable API.

## Explicit loading and schema

The caller passes exactly one config path to `load_config(Path(...))`. There is
no config discovery, environment-variable configuration, credential discovery,
fallback file, default Salesforce org, or directory creation. A relative config
filename is interpreted from the caller's working directory; paths *inside* it
are resolved from the config file's resolved parent directory. A symlinked config
therefore uses its target's directory internally. Public lifecycle commands
refuse symlinked configs through their stricter publication guards. Loading opens only that config file;
path resolution may inspect filesystem path components, without reading source
files, templates, notes, or state.

UTF-8 TOML is limited to 65,536 bytes. Duplicate keys, malformed TOML, unknown
keys/tables at any level, wrong types, excessive parser nesting, and unsupported schema versions fail.
No parser error includes raw TOML or a potentially sensitive value. TOML has no
null literal. Omit an optional value instead of providing a placeholder null.
A missing explicit file is a configuration error; permission/read failures are
operational errors. No invalid explicit file is ignored in favor of a default.

```toml
schema_version = 1
workspace_id = "demo-org"
vault = "./DemoKnowledge"

[source]
mode = "local"
project = "./sample-sfdx"

[layout]
apex_classes = "Custom Code/Apex Classes"
dashboards = "Dashboards"

[options]
include_namespaced = false
include_audit_names = true

# Optional explicit override root; internal candidate rendering only (Thread 07).
[templates]
directory = "./demo-templates"
```

| Table | Accepted keys and requirements |
| --- | --- |
| Root | Required `schema_version` (integer exactly 1), `workspace_id`, `vault`, `source`; optional `layout`, `options`, `templates` |
| `source` | Required `mode`; local requires `project` and forbids `org`; live requires `org` and forbids `project` |
| `layout` | Optional `apex_classes`, `dashboards`; defaults shown above |
| `options` | Optional boolean `include_namespaced` (false), `include_audit_names` (true); explicit false is retained |
| `templates` | When present, requires only `directory`; an empty table is invalid |

`workspace_id` contains 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens.
Strings cannot be empty, have surrounding whitespace, or contain control
characters. Arbitrary Salesforce field/type selection, command configuration,
credentials, API versions, logging, and force-overwrite settings are unsupported
config keys. The supported component type is ApexClass only. Optional internal
name filters in the normalized selection record are not exposed config options.

## Paths and selectors

`vault`, `source.project`, and `templates.directory` accept native absolute paths
or config-relative paths. `..` in these root paths resolves normally; it does not
permit traversal in generated relative paths. `~`, `$` and `%` expansion forms
are rejected; use literal paths. Non-native drive/backslash paths fail rather
than being interpreted as local relative names. Paths need not exist at this
stage. Loading does not validate an SFDX project or contact Salesforce.
Windows unrooted relative paths may use native backslashes (for example,
`..\Team Space\Config with spaces.toml`) or forward slashes. This applies to the
explicit CLI config argument too; it is relative to cwd. Drive-relative
`C:Config.toml` and current-drive-rooted `\Config.toml` or `/Config.toml` are
ambiguous and refused. POSIX still refuses Windows relative backslash syntax.
The public lexical ancestor, spelling, overlap and filesystem guards remain.
The separate [offline acquisition](OFFLINE_SOURCE.md) phase validates declared
DX package roots and supported Apex pairs using the loaded project path,
logical workspace binding, and explicit namespace selection.

Layout directories and note-state paths use `/`, remain relative to the vault,
and reject empty/`.`/`..` segments, drive/absolute paths, backslashes, control
characters, Windows reserved device names, invalid Windows filename characters,
and trailing dots/spaces. These relative paths also exclude `.git`, `.obsidian`,
and `.obforce` control-directory segments. Root paths are resolved before overlap
checks: vault and source/template roots must be disjoint, and config cannot be inside the
vault. This is an early refusal, not a safe-write certification. Repository
separation, links/junctions, special files, collisions, permissions, parent
changes, and concurrency must be checked again by later publication threads.

For example, `/fictional/work/obforce.toml` with `project = "./sample-sfdx"`
means `/fictional/work/sample-sfdx` regardless of the caller's working directory.
For a live config, replace the whole source table with:

```toml
[source]
mode = "live"
org = "fictional-sandbox"
```

Live targets must be explicit, nonempty, and cannot begin with `-`. The selector
is an alias/username for the internal [live adapter](LIVE_SOURCE.md), not verified
org identity or permission to query it. Loading never inspects authentication or invokes `sf`.

Precedence for supported selection is explicit invocation, config, then listed
non-selector defaults. Future initialization requires exactly one absolute
project path or live target; both or neither fail. Given a config, only a live
`org` override is supported. A project override or local/live switch fails.
The adapter verifies the actual org ID with a minimal query before inventory;
the live override must subsequently match the verified state org binding; an
alias change alone does not establish a new source. No rebinding workflow is
implemented. See [coverage and identity](COVERAGE.md).

## Errors and exits

Typed internal exceptions use Click's existing exception display/exit protocol.
The public Thread 12 commands use the same typed errors. Offline tests exercise
operational/config/conflict/coverage outcomes without real source access.
Callers provide concise safe diagnostics, never raw responses or note content.

| Code | Meaning | Error type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Complete selected operation or valid no-op | Success outcome |
| 1 | Operational/read/process failure | `OperationalError` |
| 2 | Invalid usage, config, or normalized input | Click usage errors, `ConfigError`, `ModelError` |
| 3 | Ownership/identity conflict or recovery required | `ConflictError` |
| 4 | Completed operation with requested incomplete/unavailable coverage | `CoverageError` or coverage outcome |

Normally validation stops at the first failing phase. If outcomes must be
combined, precedence is **3, 2, 1, 4, 0**, independent of encounter order or numeric
magnitude. Recovery/conflicts must not be hidden by a later generic failure.
A truncated requested live inventory cannot return success. By-design offline
audit/dependency exclusions are reported explicitly but do not alone force 4.
See [the independent coverage contract](COVERAGE.md).

The internal [renderer](RENDERING.md) now loads only the two documented known
assets from this explicit root, falling back per absent file to installed defaults.
Invalid existing overrides refuse. No public generation command is introduced.


Thread 08 [parses and patches caller-supplied note bytes](NOTE_FORMAT.md#internal-existing-note-parsing-and-preservation-thread-08)
using in-memory state/baselines only. It adds no config keys, command, file loading
or vault discovery. Unsupported/edited managed content raises redacted conflict
3; invalid caller contracts use 2. Existing precedence and source controls remain.


Thread 09 separately accepts explicit absolute vault/state paths and normalized
binding/selection for internal [read-only reconciliation](SYNC_SAFETY.md). It never
loads/discovers config, resolves auth/default orgs, or uses cwd/home discovery.
The caller must supply disjoint source/template/application roots for overlap
refusal and independently verified canonical org identity for live bindings.
No public config/state initialization or migration command is added.

Thread 10's internal `plan_changes` takes explicit normalized source/coverage/
graph inputs and absolute vault/state/excluded roots. Templates are already
loaded explicit assets; no config/source/template/auth discovery occurs during
planning. Existing saved graph and retained absent-component facts are explicit

`report_plan` returns text/outcome without printing or writing. No new config
key or public command is introduced; outcome precedence remains 3, 2, 1, 4, 0.

Thread 11 adds internal transaction/recovery calls with explicit absolute paths and
caller-supplied planner inputs. No config key, discovery, public command or auth
access is added. A persistent private writer.lock may remain after an actual
transaction; no-op and both previews create nothing. Recovery receives explicit
vault/state/excluded roots and reads only validated local journal evidence. See
[transaction safety](SYNC_SAFETY.md#thread-11-pre-implementation-transaction-contract--20-october-2026).

## Public initialization and initial build (Thread 12)

Thread 12 implements the first-build journey. Thread 13 adds [refresh](REFRESH.md).
All commands are noninteractive. `--config` is always required; there is no search
of cwd, parents, home, environment, auth or existing vaults.

```sh
obforce init --config ./obforce.toml --source ./FictionalProject --vault ../Knowledge --workspace-id fictional
obforce init --config ./preview.toml --org fictional-sandbox --vault ../OtherKnowledge --workspace-id fictional --dry-run
obforce build --config ./obforce.toml --dry-run
obforce build --config ./obforce.toml
obforce recover --config ./obforce.toml
obforce recover --config ./obforce.toml --rollback
obforce recover --config ./obforce.toml --cleanup
```

Exactly one `init` source selector is required: `--source PATH` or `--org TARGET`.
The config filename is invocation-relative; source/vault arguments are relative
to the config parent, including normal `..` roots. Native absolute paths are also
accepted. No expansion is added. Init preserves the accepted layout/options
(default audit names true, namespaces false); edit a valid config explicitly to
change these or select a known template override. Init validates selection and
paths without acquiring source metadata. A missing source can be configured but
will fail acquisition during build. Its config parent must already exist.

Init serializes escaped UTF-8 TOML values, validates the complete bytes through
the same strict schema, and creates one file exclusively with requested mode
0600. Any existing entry refuses. It never replaces a file or creates config
parents. A failure after exclusive creation may retain partial config evidence;
inspect it manually rather than overwrite it. `--dry-run` creates nothing.

Build uses the configured source. `--org TARGET` may override only a live source;
it never changes mode or workspace. Live builds, including previews, additionally
require both `--sf-executable ABSOLUTE_PATH` and `--sf-directory ABSOLUTE_PATH`.
The latter is an existing neutral directory disjoint from source/template/vault/
config/application roots. There is no executable search. Actual org identity is
verified by the accepted live adapter before graph and note planning. Real
operations require the user's authorization; implementation/tests used mocks only.
Windows sf remains refused; no wrapper or launcher workaround is added. The CLI
may change its own auth/cache/config state during authorized read queries; see
[the unchanged transport boundary](SF_CLI.md). Offline rejects live process options.

Build requires an absent or completely empty destination. All entries, including
hidden files, `.obsidian`, state, managed notes and a retained writer lock, block
initial build. It never adopts or resumes a vault. See [setup and recovery safety](SYNC_SAFETY.md#public-initial-setup-and-recovery-thread-12).
Missing destination/parents can be previewed without creation. Actual setup creates
at most 32 guarded portable directories before a freshly validated existing-vault
transaction. Refused publication can leave explicit setup/control evidence; do
not delete it automatically or retry build as a recovery operation.

Recover defaults to read-only validated preview. `--dry-run`, `--rollback`, and
`--cleanup` are mutually exclusive. Rollback applies only before recorded commit;
cleanup applies only to committed/cleaning evidence. Selection is rechecked under
the existing continuous writer lock. Recovery never collects source/templates,
invokes sf, discovers auth or reconstructs graph evidence. Missing source metadata
does not prevent recovery. No-op and previews preserve exact bytes/mtimes.

Reports contain fixed categories, bounded counts and independent coverage states,
including requested flags and warning counts. Precedence remains **3, 2, 1, 4, 0**.
Public recovery-required failures use 3 even when the internal writer retains an
original operational outcome; a valid recovery preview returns 0 with an explicit
recovery-required flag. Partial requested coverage can publish a first build with
4 and never proves absence. By-design offline audit/relationship exclusions alone
allow 0. State/journal bounds and schema-1 journal refusal remain unchanged.


Thread 12's Windows correction retains each original lexical spelling as well as
the resolved path. A resolver returning stored `VAULT` for requested `Vault` must
not erase the alias refusal. Every original segment receives the same bounded
parent-name comparison used for resolved paths, with ordinal string comparison
independent of native Path equality. This applies to config/source/template/vault
roots and missing suffixes in init/build/recover, including previews. No retry,
case normalization workaround, relaxed observation or new skip is added.


## Public refresh and private evidence (Thread 13)

`sync --config PATH [--dry-run]` requires existing managed state-document schema 2
with evidence schema 1. No automatic schema-1 upgrade/adoption is offered. NoteState
remains schema 1; journal schema 2 retains explicit legacy recovery support.
No config schema/key changes are made.

Live-only build accepts optional `--inventory-scope-id ID`. Sync accepts a matching
ID and `--attest-comparable-inventory` for this invocation's continuity assertion.
The attestation requires an explicit ID established at build; null declarations
cannot be initialized later. Offline rejects both flags. Existing explicit live
process paths/org verification rules apply. Missing transitions additionally need
complete supported comparable inventory; unknown continuity preserves absence and
reports incomplete evaluation. See [the full contract](REFRESH.md).


## Protected native dashboard (Thread 14)

Public build/sync now include one `Apex Classes.base` under `layout.dashboards`
(default `Dashboards`). No config key/schema change or additional command.
The whole file has exact saved ownership in an optional dashboard-schema-1
record within evidence-bearing state-document schema 2. Editing/moving/removing
it or changing its configured directory blocks the whole batch. A valid Thread
13 vault can add it only at an absent destination; no file adoption or note
migration. See [dashboard behavior, limits and recovery](DASHBOARDS.md).

MTF-2 adds no configuration knobs: new notes use Boolean `technical_debt: false`,
blank `tech_debt_severity`/`tech_debt_status`, and blank `last_reviewed`.
These human fields remain creation-only and are not backfilled on existing notes.
Available audit timestamps additionally supply reserved UTC `sf_created` and
`sf_last_modified` dates. Lifecycle stays in notes but leaves the default table.


## Qualification of refusal diagnostics

Readability checks for CLI path options are performed by the existing guarded
engine/transport reads. Click converts native paths without echoing them in a
preliminary unreadable-path error. A denied config read is operational 1 with
fixed redacted text; missing/invalid config remains input 2 and ownership conflicts
remain 3. This does not weaken filesystem checks or authorize a live operation.
[Qualification](QUALIFICATION.md) records native versus injected evidence.

# Normalized identity and coverage

Thread 13 [public refresh](REFRESH.md) loads exact private prior component/graph
evidence from state-document schema 2 rather than reconstructing it from hashes.
Missing evaluation additionally requires an immutable declared live scope and this
invocation's explicit comparability attestation; verified org/Selection and current
exhaustion alone cannot prove permission continuity. Independent coverage records,
semantic hashes and source-key identity retain the contracts below.

Thread 02 supplies immutable internal records, canonical serialization/hashing,
and validation helpers. Thread 03 now implements the internal
[offline Apex source](OFFLINE_SOURCE.md), using these unchanged contracts.
Thread 05 implements the internal [live Apex adapter](LIVE_SOURCE.md) with mocked
process tests, verified org binding, bounded enumeration and optional scoped audit
names. Thread 06 adds internal [platform relationship probes and graph construction](RELATIONSHIPS.md),
with explicit partial/unavailable coverage and synthetic tests.
All examples below are fictional. These are
versioned internal contracts, not a stable public Python API.

## Records and identities

| Record | Version-one contents |
| --- | --- |
| `SourceBinding` | Workspace ID, `local`/`live` mode, verified live org ID or null |
| `ComponentKey` | Workspace, literal `ApexClass`, namespace, full name |
| `Component` | Binding/key, optional live record ID, allowlisted facts and field availability, sorted provenance labels, optional incidental collection time |
| `Selection` | ApexClass type, explicit namespace inclusion, sorted optional internal full-name filters |
| `CollectionCoverage` | One dimension's status, method, request intent, pagination, limit result, API version, sorted warnings |
| `Coverage` | Binding/selection plus independent inventory, audit, relationship coverage |
| `Relationship` | Directed source/resolved target keys or an unresolved target label, kind, evidence method, coverage, stale flag |
| `NoteState` | Persistent UUID, binding/key, relative note path, source/graph/render hashes, exact generated-property baseline and region hash, state schema |

Model version is 1. Canonical component identity is structured JSON, for example:

```json
["demo-org","ApexClass",null,"DemoService"]
```

This avoids delimiter collisions. Identity preserves case, namespace, and Unicode
code points: `DemoService`, `demoservice`, and a namespaced class remain distinct.
An empty namespace normalizes to null. Filename equivalence is a separate
constraint: supplied note paths collide conservatively under NFC normalization
plus casefold, including on a host whose filesystem permits both names.

Duplicate component keys, duplicate live record-ID mappings, note IDs, note-key
mappings, or equivalent paths cause conflict; identical duplicates are refused
too. A record ID supplements the source key and never changes it into a filename.
Similar names/text do not establish a rename. A persistent note UUID survives a
unique move; Thread 09 [reconciles explicit read-only vault observations](SYNC_SAFETY.md)
without changing these supplied-record validators.

Bindings contain no machine path or live alias. A local workspace is the explicit
configured logical identity; moving its checkout does not inherently change it.
The live adapter supplies the actual verified org ID from a minimal Organization
query. Merely constructing a binding does not verify an ID. `require_same_source` refuses workspace, mode,
or verified-org changes. Local/live rebinding and automatic adoption are
unsupported. Changing local scope cannot establish live absence/deletion.

## Field availability and allowed facts

Normalized component attributes are exactly `api_version`, `status`, `created_at`,
`created_by`, `last_modified_at`, and `last_modified_by`. Additional raw API fields,
class bodies, endpoints, arbitrary business data, and credentials are rejected.
Adapters must normalize values before constructing records; this model does not
implement Salesforce field validation or API response parsing.

An attribute omitted from the mapping is **absent**. A present field is one of:

```json
{"availability":"unavailable","value":null}
{"availability":"null","value":null}
{"availability":"value","value":false}
{"availability":"value","value":""}
{"availability":"value","value":[]}
```

These are all different, as is integer zero. Available values can be strings,
booleans, integers, or immutable ordered tuples of strings (serialized as arrays).
Use strings for decimal API versions and normalized audit dates. Null is an
explicitly observed null; unavailable means not obtainable/collected, without
inventing a value. No filesystem or Git date becomes a Salesforce audit date.
Technical debt remains a user decision; an unset assessment is never false.

## Independent collection coverage

Each dimension uses `complete`, `partial`, `unavailable`, or `not_collected`.
`requested` records whether that dimension was part of the requested operation.
Methods, API versions, warnings, and evidence remain explicit. `pagination` is
`not_applicable`, `exhausted`, `incomplete`, or `unknown`; `limit_reached` is false,
true, or null when unknown. Complete requires positive exhaustion/non-applicability
and `limit_reached = false`. A successful process or empty array proves neither.

An offline result can have complete inventory **for the declared local scope**,
unavailable audit, and uncollected relationships by design, with the latter two
marked `requested = false`. Its status is successful with limitations reported.
If an explicitly requested dimension is partial/unavailable/uncollected, the
coverage outcome is 4. Operational failures and conflicts take precedence as
specified in [configuration](CONFIGURATION.md).

The scope fingerprint includes model version, binding, ApexClass selection,
namespace inclusion, and internal name filters. It excludes collection outcomes;
therefore a complete and partial result may share scope, but their full coverage
records differ. Namespace exclusion is explicit and must be reported. Complete
inventory alone never means complete audit or dependency coverage. Later threads
must also verify accessible comparable scope before marking a component missing;
Thread 02 implements no missing/deletion planner.

Platform-reported references are evidence of reported relationships, not proof
of runtime behavior or comprehensive impact analysis. Unresolved endpoints stay
labeled text and do not create component notes. Offline XML alone supplies no
Apex code-reference proof. Failed refreshes must preserve prior edges as stale;
the Thread 06 graph layer performs matching-source/scope stale preservation in memory.
Thread 04 process contracts and Thread 05 inventory/audit capabilities/limits are
documented in [SF_CLI.md](SF_CLI.md) and [LIVE_SOURCE.md](LIVE_SOURCE.md).
The [relationship adapter](RELATIONSHIPS.md) never claims complete platform coverage: current
MCD restrictions prevent independent exhaustion proof under the fixed allowlist.
Unresolved referencing endpoints use graph-specific evidence records; frozen
Relationship/source/scope/hash contracts remain unchanged.

## Deterministic fingerprints

`canonical_json` accepts null, strings, booleans, integers, string-keyed dicts,
and lists/tuples. It emits compact JSON with sorted object keys, literal Unicode,
and UTF-8 hashing using SHA-256 lowercase hexadecimal digests. Floats (including
NaN/infinity), sets, paths, custom objects, and non-string object keys are refused.
Do not silently stringify unsupported values. Arrays retain order; constructors
explicitly sort unordered filters/provenance/warnings. Duplicate entries are
refused rather than silently merged.

Component source hashes include model version, binding, structured key, optional
record ID, allowlisted field values/availability, and normalized provenance
labels. They exclude collection timestamps; real audit-date changes remain
semantic changes. Callers pass method labels, never host paths or incidental
CLI data, as provenance. The inventory hash sorts validated components by key,
so response ordering does not matter. An empty inventory hash does not prove a
complete scan; coverage is always separate.

The graph fingerprint sorts supplied relationship evidence and relevant resolved
note paths. Direction, incoming/outgoing edges, coverage, staleness, unresolved
labels, or a target move can change it without changing a component's own source
hash. The Thread 06 graph layer supplies relevant incident edges/locations and composes
this unchanged helper with unresolved-source descriptors and independent coverage;
the helper itself does not collect or derive edges. Exact duplicate evidence is refused.

The generated render fingerprint includes source/graph fingerprints, generated
template content hash, model/note/marker/renderer versions, layout directories,
and namespace/audit-name options. No template directory path or mtime participates.
A separate `creation_fingerprint` combines it with a creation-template content
hash for **new-note candidates only**. Save the generated-only fingerprint in
note state even on initial creation, so a creation-template edit never invalidates
existing notes. No hashes grant permission to overwrite an edited baseline.
Hash equality is an integrity aid, not authentication, encryption, or proof of
safe publication. See [note ownership](NOTE_FORMAT.md).

## Candidate rendering boundary

Thread 07 [renders internal candidates](RENDERING.md) with these unchanged records.
It retains the accepted source and graph hashes and composes the per-note graph
digest with full independent Coverage for the existing render helper graph input.
This catches inventory/audit-only coverage changes without altering source hashes
or graph helper contracts. It does not publish or authorize overwriting baselines.


Thread 08's in-memory patcher preserves these source/graph/render/creation hash
contracts and renderer-local independent-Coverage composition. It compares saved
owned-property values and exact generated bytes even when incoming hashes match.
The patch's region hash covers actual output line endings, including CRLF; it
may differ from the renderer's LF region hash. No coverage outcome grants
overwrite permission. See [supported preservation](NOTE_FORMAT.md#internal-existing-note-parsing-and-preservation-thread-08).


Thread 09 retains saved binding/Selection/scope hash separately from independent
collection outcomes. Exact selection or source rebinding mismatches refuse.
It accepts no source inventory and makes no absence/deletion/lifecycle decisions.
A vanished tracked note is an ownership conflict; an unobserved source component
is a different question for later planning. Move results retain saved hashes
and provide paths/old-new changes for existing graph/renderer invalidation.

## Thread 10 planning and absence

The internal [planner](SYNC_SAFETY.md#thread-10-pre-implementation-planner-contract--20-october-2026)
requires exact saved binding/selection and independently verified live org ID.
The explicit `comparable_live_inventory` attestation defaults false and describes
accessible scope, independently of collection status. Missing proposals require
that attestation, current complete exhausted/no-limit/no-warning inventory using
`live-apex-keyset-v1`, and matching saved method/API-version evidence. Local,
partial, unavailable, changed-method/version or noncomparable inventory retains
prior lifecycle. A vanished tracked file always conflicts. No notes are deleted.

Every tracked component absent from current inventory requires explicit retained
normalized facts matching its saved source hash. Every existing plan also requires
a previous graph whose incident hashes/paths and coverage match saved state.
The planner uses accepted stale refresh semantics and re-renders all retained
notes against reconciled paths and independent current coverage. It never turns
empty platform probes into complete relationships or offline XML into edges.
Reports show each coverage dimension independently with fixed safe warnings/status
and counts; raw warning text and audit identities stay out of diagnostics.

Thread 11 can publish a valid partial-coverage plan and retains outcome 4. It does
not use partial/offline/unavailable coverage as proof of absence or deletion.
Conflict/invalid/operational outcomes retain precedence 3, 2, 1, 4, 0; transaction
recovery acquires no source data and restores exact saved coverage with the prior
state when ownership permits rollback.

Thread 12 public initial build carries these same independent records through
source, graph, rendering, planning and publication. Reports include each status,
requested flag and warning count. Offline exclusions alone permit 0; a bounded
partial local inventory or requested partial/unavailable live facet yields 4 on
completed publication/preview. Identity ambiguity can stop before any write with
4; conflict/recovery, invalid input and operational errors retain precedence
3,2,1 over coverage. Public initial build never marks a component missing or
reactivated. No graph snapshot is stored or reconstructed from saved hashes.


## Synthetic scale evidence

Thread 15 measures a seeded 1,000-class/10,000-edge graph separately from source
collection and publication. Those edges are explicit synthetic inputs, labeled
partial; no local source text or clean empty platform reply creates dependency
facts. Mocked live inventory/audit acquisition is batched, while the fixed
relationship collector retains its 101-query budget and partial/unavailable
coverage. Its per-ID probes do not collect the complete synthetic graph.
[Qualification](QUALIFICATION.md) reports elapsed time, the exact environment,
Python traced allocations separately from whole-process RSS, refused bounds,
observed hosted results and remaining unavailable native checks. Thread 15's
selected matrix passed in run `40721222520`, attempt 2; skips and unperformed
native/live operations remain gaps. None is a throughput or service-level promise.

# Native Apex Classes dashboard

Build creates `Dashboards/Apex Classes.base` by default. Open it yourself in an
Obsidian installation with the native Bases feature available. Obforce never
launches Obsidian, enables features, installs plugins or changes `.obsidian`.
Ordinary Markdown notes, human sections, properties and links remain useful
without dashboards, Dataview, Obsidian CLI or community plugins.

The table includes a **Class** link labeled with the class name, Namespace,
Metadata Status, API Version, Created, Last Modified, Technical Debt, Debt
Severity, Debt Status and Last Reviewed. Links use each file's current location,
including uniquely moved notes. API Version uses the stored text value (`67.0`),
without adding quote characters. YAML quotes delimit that value in note source.
Missing audit dates stay blank; filesystem dates are not Salesforce audit dates.
Read each note's Coverage section for independent inventory/audit/relationship
limitations. `sf_lifecycle` remains in notes for accepted active/missing behavior,
but is omitted from the default table. Missing means unobserved in a comparable
accessible scope, not deletion; it differs from Salesforce Metadata Status.

Filtering uses Markdown plus reserved `obforce_id`, `obforce_schema: 1`, and
`sf_type: ApexClass`. Changing your `type` or `tags` does not hide a managed note.
The view is a convenience; its filter does not establish filesystem ownership.
Technical Debt uses the actual `technical_debt` property, suitable for a native
checkbox. Per maintainer finding MTF-2, new notes default to Boolean `false`
(unchecked); that initial default is not a metadata-derived assessment. Only
Boolean creation overrides are accepted. The maintainer explicitly replaced the
earlier unassessed-default proposal for this unreleased, fictional dataset:
examples and test baselines now use false, with one table and no legacy view.
Human Boolean decisions remain user-owned during generated-only refresh.

New notes also initialize user-owned `tech_debt_severity: ""`,
`tech_debt_status: ""` and `last_reviewed: null`. Recommend `High`, `Medium` or
`Low` severity; enter a review date as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Existing notes are never
backfilled, renamed or converted: earlier `technical_debt_severity`,
`technical_debt_status`, `technical_debt_review_date` and all other human fields
stay yours. The new columns use only the requested new names. Metadata never
sets severity, status or review dates. Created/Last Modified use reserved
`sf_created`/`sf_last_modified`, UTC date-only projections of available valid
Salesforce audit timestamps. The original `sf_*_at` values remain available.

Obsidian property types are vault-wide. If your vault already assigns another
type, you can review it yourself in Obsidian: Checkbox for `technical_debt`, Date
for the date properties, Text for API Version and human severity/status. Obforce
never changes property-type settings. Automated checks do not validate native
display or existing vault property-type interactions.

The literal packaged YAML uses documented filters, formulas and table columns.
See official [syntax](https://obsidian.md/help/bases/syntax),
[functions](https://obsidian.md/help/bases/functions) and
[table documentation](https://obsidian.md/help/bases/views/table) and
[property types](https://obsidian.md/help/properties), read on
26 October 2026. Automated schema/predicate tests do not constitute native
Obsidian preview or rendering acceptance. The maintainer's original manual
observation is recorded as MTF-2. Optional native preview remained unavailable to
the agent; no real vault or app was opened by the agent. Thread 14 is accepted
and #14 closed after exact-merge run `40517073513`, attempt 1, passed all 12 cells
and 24 independent installs at correction `6d08696` / merge `cdf0e68`. See
[acceptance and retained evidence limits](../dev/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md#thread-14-acceptance-and-closure--27-october-2026).
This does not establish a native rendering result.

## Destination and ownership

The existing config setting controls the parent directory:

```toml
[layout]
apex_classes = "Custom Code/Apex Classes"
dashboards = "Dashboards"
```

The filename is fixed: `Apex Classes.base`. One dashboard participates in every
public build/sync. No new config key, lifecycle command or template override exists.
After creation, changing the configured dashboard directory refuses; Obforce does
not infer a dashboard move, copy it to a second location or remove the old file.

The whole generated `.base` file is protected, including layout edits made by
Obsidian's UI. Current bytes must exactly match saved bytes before any batch can
publish. Edits, missing/moved files, duplicate managed indicators, unowned targets
(even identical content), links/hard links/reparse points, unsafe parents or
portable spelling collisions return conflict 3. One dashboard or note conflict
blocks all note, dashboard and state changes. Preserve your edits and resolve
ownership before running another preview; there is no reset, overwrite, adoption
or repair mode. For a custom view, author a separate indicator-free Base at another
path and retain the generated file unchanged. Do not copy its reserved
`obforce:dashboard` ownership comment into a user-managed view.

Valid Thread 13 state-document-schema-2 vaults have no dashboard record. Their
first sync creates the new dashboard only when its destination is absent and
there is no untracked managed dashboard indicator. It preserves existing UUIDs,
notes and human fields. It never adopts an existing file. Evidence-less legacy
sync remains refused, and build still requires an absent/empty destination.
This adds an asset, without migrating notes or reconstructing prior evidence.

## State, recovery and previews

An optional exact-shape root `dashboard` record extends evidence-bearing state
schema 2. It has `dashboard_schema: 1`, a portable relative `path`, `content_hash`
(SHA-256) and canonical base64 `content` holding exact bytes. No human note data
is added. Evidence schema 1, NoteState schema 1 and journal schema 2 remain;
MTF-2 advances the renderer fingerprint to version 4 for date projections.
Older executables reject the extra state key/new reserved date properties; use this version
for these vaults and recovery. Unknown keys/versions/types or corrupt baselines
refuse. See [the recorded contract](../dev/THREAD_14_DASHBOARD_CONTRACT.md).

Changed notes, dashboard, then complete state use the same recoverable writer.
The dashboard has the same full pathname/historical descriptor/hash/absence/parent
checks and continuous writer lock. Precommit rollback restores prior bytes/state,
or removes only a proven newly created asset; committed cleanup removes only
transaction-owned temporary material. Intervening edits retain evidence and
refuse. Valid old note-only journal-schema-2 recovery remains supported;
journal schema 1 remains refused. No atomic multi-file, hostile-race, power-loss
or Windows Salesforce execution guarantee is added.

```sh
obforce sync --config "./Demo Config.toml" --dry-run
obforce sync --config "./Demo Config.toml"
obforce recover --config "./Demo Config.toml"
```

Recovery preview names the phase-compatible `--rollback` or `--cleanup` operation.
Review it before applying that operation with the same explicit config. Ambiguous
or incomplete evidence needs manual resolution, without deleting control files to
bypass checks. All previews create no Obforce files/directories. Unchanged
notes/dashboard/state preserve exact bytes/mtimes; reads may update access times.

One dashboard is limited to 16 KiB. Every discovered `.base` is read under that
ceiling and the shared 64 MiB aggregate read ceiling. State remains at most
16 MiB; the dashboard counts inside the existing 128 changed-file, 32 MiB
before-plus-after transaction and 64 MiB candidate limits. All other entry,
path, JSON, parent and guard limits still apply. Bounds refuse, never truncate.
Reports distinguish note actions, dashboard action, state-file changes and total
changed files. Init's file count is its new config; recovery counts journaled
files; no-op is zero. Counts and coverage explanations stay bounded and omit
private names/paths/audit identities/raw warnings. Exit precedence is **3,2,1,4,0**.
Optional verbose enhancement #19 remains unstarted.

Try the [fictional quickstart](QUICKSTART.md). A read-only
[presentation sample](../examples/sample_vault/README.md) contains no private
state and is not a build/sync target. Actual local/hosted/native evidence and
acceptance status are recorded in the [roadmap](../dev/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md).

# Internal live Apex inventory and audit adapter

Thread 05 implements `sources/live.py`, tested with synthetic CLI envelopes and
mocked process collection only. It adds no public command, authentication,
renderer, state adoption, deletion planner, or vault writes. A separately invoked
Thread 06 [relationship adapter](RELATIONSHIPS.md) now consumes normalized live
inventory and reverifies identity; `collect_live` itself still leaves relationships
uncollected.
Internal interfaces are not a stable Python API. Thread 12 connects the adapter to explicit public initial build;
see [configuration](CONFIGURATION.md#public-initialization-and-initial-build-thread-12). Windows `sf` execution remains refused by the unchanged
[process boundary](SF_CLI.md); [enhancement #18](https://github.com/jeffshurtliff/obforce/issues/18)
is outside v0.1.0 and is not a prerequisite for this adapter.

Thread 05 is accepted and delivered at merge `85ba7cd`. Exact-commit
[run 39325616681, attempt 1](https://github.com/jeffshurtliff/obforce/actions/runs/39325616681)
passed all 12 Linux/macOS/Windows Python 3.12–3.15 cells: Linux/macOS each
reported 441 passed; Windows each reported 430 passed/11 expected skips. Every
cell passed standalone checks, fresh build/Twine and both independent artifact
installations. The Windows skips cover nine POSIX collector cases, the POSIX
wrapper-symlink case and the unavailable FIFO case. Mocked adapter/refusal checks
and hosted Windows results do not qualify Windows sf execution. See the
[acceptance record](../dev/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md#thread-05-acceptance-and-closure--19-october-2026).
Thread 06 is accepted at merge `2aa8d2b` with all 12 exact-merge hosted cells
passing; its [relationship adapter documentation](RELATIONSHIPS.md) retains the
partial/unavailable coverage limitation. Subsequent renderer/planner/writer increments are accepted; Thread 12 now
composes the adapter into initial build with mocked live orchestration only.
Thread 13 and later and enhancement #18 remain NOT STARTED.

## Invocation and verified identity

The internal caller supplies the explicit absolute trusted executable, existing
neutral working directory, target, logical workspace, existing `Selection`,
privacy option, and any previously verified configured/state `SourceBinding`.
There is no executable/default-org/auth/config/state discovery. A caller must
separately obtain authorization for the target and read operations before a real
invocation. No real CLI or org was invoked to implement or validate this thread.

The first query is ordinary `SELECT Id FROM Organization LIMIT 2`. Exactly one
valid `00D` Salesforce ID, `done=true`, matching count, no continuation, no warning
or stderr, and no unexpected result fields are required. An unavailable query is
an operational failure; ambiguous/incomplete identity evidence is coverage exit 4.
Only the ID is requested, never organization names, endpoints, credentials, or an
org-display operation. Customer Portal users cannot query Organization according
to the official reference; this adapter never attempts another identity source.

IDs use strict object prefixes, alphanumeric 15-character form or checksum-valid
18-character form, and normalize to 18 characters. The resulting existing live
binding contains workspace/mode/verified org ID, never alias. Every supplied
configured/state binding must match exactly before inventory starts; a different
workspace, mode, or org is a conflict (3), without adoption/rebinding. Bindings
supplied by callers must already use the canonical org-ID representation; this
adapter does not migrate existing state. State-document validation remains Thread
09. Missing bindings mean an initial internal collection, not permission to adopt
managed notes or reconstruct missing state.

An alias is merely the explicit CLI selector. These separate CLI calls assume a
trusted stable CLI/auth configuration and stable accessible metadata scope during
collection. Identity verification and filter pagination are observations, not an
atomic org/auth snapshot. Concurrent alias/auth/permission/metadata changes can
invalidate comparability. Complete here means exhaustion of this observed,
selected accessible scope, never whole-org visibility or deletion proof. Later
missing-note decisions still require their own comparable-scope checks.

## Fixed queries and finite enumeration

Apex inventory uses Tooling queries with exactly:

```sql
SELECT Id, Name, NamespacePrefix, ApiVersion, Status
FROM ApexClass WHERE NamespacePrefix = null ORDER BY Id LIMIT 200
```

Actual query strings are single-line. Namespace inclusion omits that predicate.
Subsequent queries add `Id > '<validated previous page final ID>'`; no raw name,
selector, namespace, endpoint or continuation string is interpolated. Server ID
ordering selects the cursor; the implementation does not invent an ID collation.
The existing optional internal `full_names` filter is applied locally to the
class Name, as in offline acquisition, and never inserted into SOQL. Selection
still distinguishes namespace in the structured component key. Unexpected
namespaces in an exclusion query are retained as a scope contradiction, excluded
from output, and block complete inventory. Duplicate component keys or canonical
record IDs, even identical records or repetitions across pages, cause conflict.

Every page must have consistent returned count/`totalSize`, `done=true`, no
continuation, warnings or stderr, and no unexpected result properties. All these
observations remain in safe `PageEvidence` records, including contradictory ones.
Only their booleans/counts/fixed diagnostic codes are retained; no warning text,
raw result or endpoint is exposed. Unknown result fields conservatively prevent
completeness. Malformed envelope types and impossible `totalSize < returned`
remain operational refusals in the accepted boundary.

A full **or short** page requires another bounded query. Inventory is complete
only after a consistent terminal empty query and consistent evidence for every
prior page, following verified identity. One empty array, successful process or
done flag alone is insufficient. Contradictory pages stop enumeration as partial;
returned valid selected rows can remain in the private result but confer no
absence/deletion evidence. A returned continuation is never executed or removed
by a later successful query. There is no arbitrary endpoint, OFFSET, bulk export,
query-file operation, shell, default target, or wrapper workaround.

| Boundary | Maximum |
| --- | --- |
| Inventory page | 200 records |
| Inventory page queries, including terminal probe | 51 |
| Enumerated records before selection | 10,000 |
| All query invocations, including identity/audit | 156 |
| Collection wall budget | 300 seconds |
| Each process wall budget | Lesser of 60 seconds and remaining collection time |
| Each process stdout | 262,144 bytes |
| Each process stderr | 65,536 bytes |

The final terminal probe fits after 50 full pages at the record ceiling. Records
beyond the ceiling are not accepted, and exhausting page/query/record/time budgets
before exhaustion returns partial inventory with explicit fixed reasons and exit
4. Limits are internal constants, not public tuning options. Existing pipe/JSON
bounds, cleanup and Windows refusal stay unchanged. Process spawning itself and
cleanup have the limitations described in [SF_CLI.md](SF_CLI.md); this deadline
does not make OS-uninterruptible operations interruptible. At most 156 bounded
outputs are processed sequentially; raw responses are not accumulated in results.
The CLI may also make its own auto-fetch and column-metadata requests internally;
156 bounds CLI invocations, not a promise about exact HTTP request consumption.

## Audit privacy, normalization and optional failures

After each inventory page, query dates only for selected validated Apex IDs:

```sql
SELECT Id, CreatedDate, LastModifiedDate FROM ApexClass WHERE Id IN ('<selected ID>')
```

When `include_audit_names=true`, a separate scoped query uses exactly
`Id, CreatedBy.Name, LastModifiedBy.Name` and the same selected Apex-ID set. The
field projection, WHERE structure and validated ID literals are generated
internally; there is no User scan/query, User ID collection, username, email,
Body, SymbolTable, FullName, Metadata, unrelated customer data or technical-debt
assessment. FullName/Metadata have per-query restrictions and are unnecessary
for the established Name/namespace identity. The CLI itself can perform column
metadata requests as documented in its official source.

Dates are strict ISO timestamps with explicit timezone, validated calendar and
offset, normalized to UTC with six fractional digits. Class ApiVersion accepts
finite integral JSON numbers or equivalent version strings and normalizes to
`N.0`, under the same 1–999 syntax as offline XML. This is the class compilation
version, **not** evidence of the API version used for the request. The transport
neither selects nor exposes a request version; coverage `api_version` stays null.
Statuses are Active/Deleted, matching offline normalization; Inactive is unused
for ApexClass in the official reference and is refused. Required identity,
namespace, version or status fields missing/malformed are validation exit 2.

The unchanged availability contract is applied deliberately:

- Name omission sends no name query and leaves `created_by`/`last_modified_by`
  **absent**; requested date coverage is still tracked.
- Missing requested audit keys/rows/nested Names are **unavailable**; requested
  display names are not inferred from IDs, aliases, auth identities or other fields.
- Explicit null date, relationship, or Name is an observed **null**, not unavailable.
- Available dates/display names are validated; unexpected projected/relationship
  fields or malformed observed values fail with safe validation diagnostics.

Optional date/name process or envelope failures become fixed `query_unavailable`
audit warnings with unavailable facts; the boundary has intentionally redacted
the raw cause, so the adapter does not guess permission loss versus unsupported
field versus timeout/authentication. No fallback query broadens access and no
retry scans Users. Partial optional envelopes retain their contradictory signals;
missing records/fields remain unavailable. An unselected audit ID or duplicate
audit mapping is a conflict. Config/model/conflict errors are not swallowed as
optional failures. Required identity/inventory failures remain operational exit
1; a later required permission failure does not return a completed collection.

Inventory, audit, and relationship coverage remain independent. Audit is complete
only if inventory is exhausted and all requested date/name queries and fields
are complete (observed null is known). With some known facts it is partial;
otherwise unavailable. Complete empty scope has vacuously complete requested
audit. Relationships are `not_collected`, `requested=false` in `collect_live`;
explicitly requested Thread 06 collection returns its own independent relationship
coverage. Any requested incomplete dimension produces outcome 4 through the
existing coverage contract. Combined errors retain precedence 3, 2, 1, 4, 0.
Consumers must inspect coverage/outcome; returned rows or their hash are never a
completeness certificate.

Source hashes use the existing component/inventory functions without contract
changes. Canonical IDs, normalized dates/version, validated facts/availability,
and fixed inventory/audit provenance labels are semantic inputs. Collection
ordering, alias, host paths, raw JSON/attributes/URLs, diagnostics and wall time
are excluded. Audit fact changes affect source hashes; name omission and
namespace/name selection remain explicit privacy/scope inputs. No fields alter
ownership, source-key identity, lifecycle, or human technical-debt decisions.

## Official contracts checked on 19 October 2026

Documentation/source reads only, without executing `sf`:

- [Current Tooling API Developer Guide](https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_tooling.pdf):
  System Fields (printed p. 55) defines Id, CreatedDate, LastModifiedDate and User
  relationships; ApexClass (pp. 111–114) defines query support, Name (255), namespace
  (15), ApiVersion, Status and the single-record FullName/Metadata restrictions.
- [Current Object Reference](https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/object_reference.pdf):
  ApexClass (pp. 574–577) corroborates fields/status; Organization (p. 4065) permits
  SELECT/query and excludes Customer Portal users. The corresponding HTML object
  pages returned no readable body, so the official PDF text was used.
- [API permission requirements](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-rest/guide/intro-rest-compatible-editions.html)
  and the Tooling guide require appropriate API/org/object access; endpoint-specific
  permission rules differ. Do not transfer ApexClassMember's View All Data/Author
  Apex requirement to ApexClass or treat successful accessible queries as whole-org
  permission certification. No permission/auth discovery is implemented.
- [Filter-based pagination guidance](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000387840&language=en_US&type=1)
  documents sorting/filter anchors including Id rather than OFFSET beyond its
  2,000-row ceiling. Applying that general guidance to the fixed ApexClass SELECTs
  is this adapter's design choice, validated with mocks, not a live qualification.
- [REST Query](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-rest/guide/resources-query.html)
  defines records/totalSize/done/nextRecordsUrl and variable batch sizes; the
  adapter checks the CLI's aggregated result rather than assuming an HTTP batch.
- [CLI query reference](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_data_query.html)
  documents explicit target/query/JSON/Tooling flags. Official
  [implementation](https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-data/blob/a0cdb671f42af74e31a782c34c5cdcc22e1ea5b0/src/commands/data/query.ts)
  and [inner result schema](https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-data/blob/a0cdb671f42af74e31a782c34c5cdcc22e1ea5b0/schemas/data-query.json)
  confirm auto-fetch/maxFetch, truncation warnings, aggregated records/count/done
  and additional column-metadata requests. Current main still resolved to that
  source commit during this review; it is not an installed CLI/version pin.

Synthetic fixture/test evidence does not establish actual Salesforce permission,
installed CLI/Node/plugin compatibility, live exhaustion, native Windows sf
execution, or full lifecycle safety. Those require separately authorized work.

Thread 07 adds internal [candidate rendering](RENDERING.md) from these normalized
records and graph results. It changes no live queries, transport, privacy controls
or Windows sf refusal, and requires no real org access to test rendering.

# Note ownership and state contract

Thread 13 [public refresh](REFRESH.md) now publishes generated-only patches and
exact source/graph evidence through the accepted writer. Its state-document
envelope is schema 2; NoteState remains schema 1 with unchanged UUID/property/body
baselines. Legacy evidence-less public refresh refuses without adoption/migration.
The dated internal increments below retain their original contract boundaries.

Thread 02 freezes constants, normalized state records, and fingerprint inputs.
Thread 07 [renders candidate strings](RENDERING.md); Thread 08 now parses and
patches caller-supplied managed-note bytes internally as described below. State
loading/discovery and unique move reconciliation are internal Thread 09 work
([safety contract](SYNC_SAFETY.md)); Thread 10 adds internal read-only planning.
Accepted Thread 11 publication/recovery is connected to public initial build by
Thread 12. Refresh remains Thread 13. This fictional note illustrates the
version-one contract; initial build never adopts or regenerates an existing note.

```markdown
---
obforce_id: "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"
obforce_schema: 1
sf_type: "ApexClass"
sf_full_name: "DemoService"
sf_source_mode: "local"
sf_dependency_coverage: "not_collected"
sf_lifecycle: "active"
type: "salesforce_component"
tags: ["salesforce"]
technical_debt: false
tech_debt_severity: ""
tech_debt_status: ""
last_reviewed: null
---

<!-- obforce:generated:start -->
## Salesforce Metadata

Fictional local-scope facts. Salesforce audit values are unavailable.
Dependencies were not collected from this offline input.
<!-- obforce:generated:end -->

## Business Context

Human-authored context belongs here.

## Known Issues / Technical Debt

Leave assessment to a person.

## Additional Information
```

## Exact ownership and versions

`obforce_id` is a persistent canonical lowercase UUID, independent of its path;
`obforce_schema` is integer 1, not a boolean or string. Model, note, state,
config, and marker versions start at 1, as does the initial renderer-contract
version. The marker version is tracked internally; it is not an extra note key.
Unsupported schemas require refusal, never automatic migration or repair.

The exact generator-owned property allowlist is:

| Identity | Salesforce facts | Collection/lifecycle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `obforce_id` | `sf_type`, `sf_full_name`, `sf_namespace` | `sf_source_mode` |
| `obforce_schema` | `sf_api_version`, `sf_status` | `sf_dependency_coverage` |
| | `sf_created_at`, `sf_created_by` | `sf_lifecycle` |
| | `sf_last_modified_at`, `sf_last_modified_by` | |
| | `sf_created`, `sf_last_modified` (UTC dates) | |

The whole `sf_*` namespace is reserved. An unknown `sf_*` key is unsupported and
must be refused rather than adopted or overwritten. Every other key belongs to
the user after creation, including `type`, `tags`, `aliases`, business fields,
all `technical_debt*` fields, and arbitrary custom properties. Creation defaults
do not transfer their ownership. MTF-2 changes new-note `technical_debt` to a strict
Boolean, false by default; this is an initial checkbox default, not an inferred
assessment. The maintainer authorized false throughout fictional/example/test
defaults, without retaining historical unassessed data or a legacy view.
New `tech_debt_severity` and `tech_debt_status` strings default blank; `last_reviewed`
defaults null, with `YYYY-MM-DD` recommended for a human review date. These and
earlier human key names are never renamed or backfilled on existing notes.

Owned property values are flat scalars or lists supported by Obsidian. Unknown
audit values are omitted and their availability explained in the generated
region. A null namespace means no namespace, not an invented package. Lifecycle
is `active` or `missing`; missing only means unobserved in a comparable complete
accessible live scope, not proven deletion. Dependency coverage uses the four
statuses in [COVERAGE.md](COVERAGE.md). Audit display names are optional via
`include_audit_names`; exclude unnecessary emails, usernames, org/record IDs,
internal URLs, raw API data, and class bodies from notes. Quote wikilinks when
stored as YAML values. Serialization/escaping is implemented for new candidates in Thread 07.

## Generated region

The exact reserved marker strings are:

```text
<!-- obforce:generated:start -->
<!-- obforce:generated:end -->
```

There must be exactly one ordered pair, each on its own line. Repeated, nested,
missing, reversed, inline, or otherwise malformed markers are conflicts. Marker
strings may not occur in source values or template content in a way that creates
an extra marker or ambiguous boundary. Thread 07 validates its own generated/new candidates against this structure;
Thread 08 independently validates supplied existing bytes too.

Only the bytes strictly between the validated marker lines are replaceable.
Preserve the marker lines and all user body bytes outside them, including line
endings. A creation template initializes new notes and user sections. Refresh
must never render the whole existing note from that template.

Generated properties and the generated body each have saved baselines. An edit
to either is a conflict even when Salesforce facts are unchanged. Identity edits,
duplicate IDs/mappings, unknown schema, invalid markers, duplicate YAML keys,
unsafe tags, malformed frontmatter, and unsupported YAML structures block the
batch before any publication. No fallback destructive repair or force mode.
User prose and supported custom YAML structure/comments/types/quoting must be
preserved. Universal byte-identical frontmatter preservation is not promised;
Thread 08 supports the bounded round-trip forms below and refuses unsafe forms.

## Internal state and invalidation

`NoteState` stores UUID, binding, structured component key, portable vault-relative
path using `/`, source/graph/generated-render hashes, exact owned-property
baseline, and generated-region SHA-256. Baseline values use the normalized
availability wrapper, distinguishing an absent key, null, empty, false, and
unavailable. Identity/schema baseline entries must exactly match the note UUID
and supported note schema. User-owned properties are forbidden in that baseline.

Mappings are copied and read-only so callers cannot mutate a previously hashed
record. State schema/UUID/path/digest validation exists for supplied records.
The private `.obforce/state.json` wire envelope is implemented internally in
Thread 09, including strict duplicate-key/ID/path validation, bounded loading,
missing/corrupt state refusal and identity reconciliation. It wraps the unchanged
NoteState with exact saved generated-region bytes encoded as canonical base64;
see [SYNC_SAFETY](SYNC_SAFETY.md). Constructing a `NoteState`
is not evidence of a valid discovered vault or safe recovery state.

A unique moved note retains its UUID and source key. Its changed path invalidates
affected links/graph/render fingerprints. Copied IDs, multiple notes for one
component, portable path collisions, edited identities, vanished managed notes,
and ambiguous mapping cause refusal rather than recreation, adoption, or deletion.
Workspace/live-org bindings cannot silently switch; see [source identity](COVERAGE.md).

Render fingerprints include all relevant graph/path, generated-template,
schema/renderer-version, layout, and privacy inputs. A separate creation-only
candidate fingerprint never replaces the generated render hash saved in state.
Collection times, host paths, and response ordering do not enter source hashes;
actual audit dates do. No-op bytes/mtimes must remain unchanged when later sync
is implemented. Notes and their state must ultimately publish through the same
recoverable transaction; per-file replacement alone is insufficient. This thread
provides no vault writes, locks, journals, recovery, or publication commands.

## Relationship invalidation boundary

Thread 06's [internal graph](RELATIONSHIPS.md) derives References and Referenced By
from one directed evidence set, retaining unresolved/unsupported endpoints as labels.
Only explicitly supplied managed-note paths can supply link locations. Graph-only
changes or a neighboring note move change graph fingerprints without changing
component facts/source hashes or note ownership. Coverage/stale changes participate
in invalidation too. Thread 07 renders these explicit mappings; Thread 08 supplies
in-memory preservation. Thread 09 adds read-only state/move discovery; publication remains later work;
this graph neither adopts notes nor writes state.

See [internal rendering](RENDERING.md) for engine-owned YAML/markers, finite Jinja
overrides, candidate bounds, separate creation/generated hashes and independent
coverage invalidation. Whole-new-note candidates must never replace existing notes.


## Internal existing-note parsing and preservation (Thread 08)

`sync/notes.py` accepts immutable caller-supplied note bytes. `parse_note` returns
an immutable observation with exact generated-region bytes and hash, properties,
and byte offsets. `patch_note` also requires a validated **in-memory** `NoteState`,
the exact saved generated-region bytes, and an accepted Thread 07
`GeneratedCandidate`. A whole `NewNoteCandidate` is refused. There is no file/path
input, state-file loading, note/vault discovery, adoption, move reconciliation,
batch planner, publication, locking, journal, recovery or public lifecycle command.
The source binding/selection and provenance of the accepted renderer candidate
remain the caller's responsibility; candidate hashes are not authentication.

The parser verifies an existing canonical lowercase UUID, integer schema 1,
the exact reserved allowlist above, and one ordered generated marker pair at
column zero on separate terminated lines. Unknown `sf_*` keys and any other
`obforce:` occurrence are ambiguous and refused, including occurrences in YAML,
inline/repeated/reversed/nested/malformed markers. It never invents an ID or
infers a rename. Identity/schema edits and source-key/mode mismatches refuse.

Before every patch, **both** current owned properties and current marker-interior
bytes must equal their saved baselines. The saved bytes must also match the
state's SHA-256. FieldValue comparisons retain exact types and presence:
absent, null, false, integer zero, empty string and empty list differ. An
unavailable baseline entry cannot stand in for a present null note property.
Even unchanged metadata, matching incoming source/render hashes, or a current
body hash matching a modified state digest cannot bypass the exact byte comparison.
There is no force mode or destructive fallback.

### Supported frontmatter and finite parsing

A note must be UTF-8 without a BOM/preamble, NUL or bare CR, starting with an exact
`---` line and ending its frontmatter with another exact `---` line. Delimiters
must be terminated. Alternate YAML document delimiters, directives and multiple
YAML documents are unsupported. Unescaped Unicode newline characters/BOM inside
frontmatter are refused; ordinary Unicode text is supported.

The root is a block mapping with simple, nonempty, single-line string keys at
column zero. Quoted keys are supported, including `"null"` and `"false"`; explicit
`?` keys, complex keys and non-string keys are refused. Duplicate keys are refused.

| Form | Supported behavior |
| --- | --- |
| User scalars | Strings, null, booleans, integers up to 64 magnitude bits, finite floats and YAML dates/datetimes; exact original spelling stays in the note |
| Owned scalars | String, null, boolean or bounded integer; strict normalized types match the existing FieldValue contract |
| Lists | Empty or strings only, flow or block; arbitrary lists/nested lists/maps are refused |
| Strings | Plain/single/double quoted, literal/folded multiline, Unicode, chomping/indentation indicators accepted by the parser |
| Comments/presentation | Supported comments, blank lines, order, quoting, indentation and multiline style in user entries are retained by leaving their source bytes untouched |
| Unsupported YAML | All explicit tags, including standard tags, anchors, aliases, merge keys, sets, binary, nested maps, nonfinite floats and arbitrary object constructors are refused |

`ruamel.yaml` is resolved by Poetry as `ruamel-yaml >=0.19.1,<0.20.0`, locked to
0.19.1 without an optional C extension. Each pass uses fresh pure Python
`YAML(typ='rt')` instances, quotes preserved and duplicate keys disabled. The
round-trip loader derives from its safe loader and adds no Python constructors.
A bounded token scan rejects references/tags/directives before loading. Streaming
events enforce depth, node and scalar limits before composition/construction;
the library's own depth guard counts scalar leaves too. Loaded values are
validated against the flat subset, never silently stringified or discarded.

| Refusal bound | Maximum |
| --- | --- |
| Input note / output note | 1 MiB each |
| Input frontmatter / output frontmatter | 64 KiB each |
| Properties | 128 |
| Scanner tokens | 8,192 |
| Parse nodes | 4,096 |
| Collection depth | 2 (root mapping plus a flat sequence) |
| Each scalar / key | 16 KiB UTF-8 |
| Each list | 1,024 strings |

Incoming candidates retain Thread 07's stricter rendering bounds, section/template
validation, scalar types, hashes and required owned identity/source fields.
Bounds refuse rather than truncate. This is finite in-process parsing, not OS
resource isolation or universal YAML support. Official contracts reviewed on
20 October 2026: [round-trip API](https://yaml.dev/doc/ruamel.yaml/api/),
[preservation details](https://yaml.dev/doc/ruamel.yaml/detail/),
[publisher metadata](https://pypi.org/project/ruamel.yaml/),
[YAML 1.2.2](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/) and
[Obsidian properties](https://obsidian.md/help/properties).

### Patch and byte policies

Round-trip node/token source spans select only changed owned values or omitted
owned key/value entries. Changed values use the accepted flat JSON-compatible
YAML encoding. Existing owned key positions remain; newly available keys append
in sorted order. Unchanged owned entries also retain their original bytes.
Comments inside replaced/deleted owned spans survive as standalone comments in
place; an unsupported comment boundary refuses. A comment attached to a deleted
owned value may therefore lose that association, while retaining its text/order.
No user entry is passed through a YAML dumper or the creation template.
This is a precise supported-subset guarantee, not universal byte-identical
frontmatter: changed/deleted/new owned entries can change spelling/spacing and
comment placement. No-op returns the original bytes object exactly. A generated-
body-only update leaves the complete frontmatter bytes untouched.

Both frontmatter (including delimiters) and the marker/interior envelope must be
individually uniform LF or CRLF. They may use different uniform conventions.
Mixed endings within either envelope refuse, including a mixed generated region
that happens to match its baseline. Mixed LF/CRLF in human body regions is allowed
and preserved verbatim. Incoming LF generated text is adapted only to the existing
marker ending. Marker-line bytes, all outside-body bytes, the final newline's
presence/absence and human whitespace remain exact; no document-wide normalization.
The returned baseline/hash cover the resulting exact interior bytes, so a CRLF
output normally differs from the renderer's LF `region_hash`.

`NotePatch` contains only candidate bytes, the next exact property/body baselines,
exact region SHA-256, unchanged candidate source/graph/render digests, and a
byte-change flag. It neither writes nor constructs a state document. The entire
candidate is reparsed and checked against incoming properties/region and retained
user values before return. All nonreserved properties remain user-owned, including
custom `type`, tags, aliases, business fields and every `technical_debt*` property.
Absent/null/false assessments, severity/status and review dates are never inferred
or replaced with creation defaults. Unavailable/absent/null incoming audits follow
the accepted renderer's omission contract: remove omitted owned keys, rather than
inventing null. Audit-name omission remains effective in properties and generated
text; human-authored content is preserved.

Malformed/unsupported notes, invalid markers, edited baselines and identity
conflicts raise concise redacted `ConflictError` (3). Invalid caller/candidate
contracts raise `ModelError` (2), with identity conflicts retaining 3. Parser
messages, note snippets and local paths are never displayed. Existing outcome
precedence stays 3, 2, 1, 4, 0. Thread 08 is accepted at implementation `d79f5e2` /
merge `dba53ab`; #8 is closed. Exact-merge run `39453887153`, attempt 1, passed all
12 Linux/macOS/Windows Python 3.12–3.15 cells: 744 passed per Linux/macOS cell,
732 passed/12 expected skips per Windows cell. Every standalone gate, fresh

[acceptance record](../dev/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md#thread-08-acceptance-and-closure--20-october-2026)
for actual evidence and retained historical failures/skips. No real sf/org/vault

all 12 cells and all 24 independent installs; see the
[acceptance record](../dev/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md#thread-09-acceptance-and-closure--20-october-2026).
Thread 10 internal read-only planning/reporting is accepted, including correction
`a2132c3` / merge `6004c35`; #10 is closed. All 12 cells and 24 independent installs
passed in exact-merge run `39510802449`, attempt 1; see the

[transaction contract](SYNC_SAFETY.md#thread-11-pre-implementation-transaction-contract--20-october-2026).
Thread 12 is implemented locally pending acceptance; Threads 13–17 and
enhancement #18 remain NOT STARTED.

Thread 10's existing-note candidates always call the preservation patcher after

the planner alone proposes missing after the positive comparable supported live

Both strict owned-property and exact saved-byte comparisons still gate changes.
