# Offline Apex acquisition

Thread 03 implements internal read-only acquisition from an explicit Salesforce
DX project. It returns the existing [normalized records](COVERAGE.md) and typed
[errors](CONFIGURATION.md#errors-and-exits). The Python interface is internal;
Thread 12 connects it to public initial build; see the fictional
[quickstart](QUICKSTART.md). Refresh remains planned.
Thread 07 adds separate internal [candidate rendering](RENDERING.md), without
changing this source or collecting offline relationships.

## Fictional example

The repository [sample project](../examples/sample_sfdx/sfdx-project.json) contains
two declared packages and two fictional Apex classes. From a development checkout:

```python
from pathlib import Path

from obforce.models import Selection, SourceBinding
from obforce.sources.local import collect_local

result = collect_local(
    Path('examples/sample_sfdx').resolve(),
    SourceBinding('fictional-workspace', 'local'),
    Selection(include_namespaced=False),
)
assert [item.key.full_name for item in result.components] == ['DemoExtension', 'DemoService']
assert result.coverage.inventory.status == 'complete'
assert result.coverage.audit.status == 'unavailable'
assert result.coverage.relationships.status == 'not_collected'
```

No `sf`, authentication, external process, schema fetch, network, or Obsidian is
used. Acquisition creates no config, vault, state, log, cache, or source files.
Normal interpreter bytecode caches can be disabled with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`.
Filesystem access times may change as an ordinary result of reading; source
bytes and modification times remain unchanged. Tests copy the sample into a
temporary directory and compare complete before/after snapshots.

## Selected local scope

The manifest must be bounded JSON with a nonempty `packageDirectories` list.
Every entry requires a portable slash-separated relative `path`; all declared
packages are scanned regardless of `default` or declaration order. The project
root is explicit and absolute; a root link/junction is refused, and its native
ancestor path is resolved once. Config loading already resolves configured root
paths; acquisition cannot reconstruct links that the caller previously resolved.
Every package must exist and be a directory inside that resolved root.

Absolute/drive paths, traversal, empty/dot segments, backslashes, reserved names,
duplicate/overlapping roots, and case/Unicode-equivalent root declarations fail.
Below the root, links, junctions/reparse points, multiply linked files, special
files, and portable filename collisions are refused, including unsupported
files. Directory enumeration/read failures refuse a result. Already observed
file/directory identities, sizes, and modification/change times are rechecked
to detect intervening changes. These checks require a stable source checkout;
they do not promise isolation from a hostile process racing filesystem operations.

For Windows path-to-descriptor comparisons, CPython can expose creation time as
pathname `st_ctime_ns` and change time as descriptor `st_ctime_ns` for the same
file ([CPython #157671](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157671)). Only an
exact integer descriptor `st_birthtime_ns` matching the pathname ctime can bridge
this difference, with device, inode, mode, size, and mtime unchanged. The raw
descriptor snapshot, including its own change time, is still compared before
and after reading; full pathname preconditions are rechecked independently.
No time rounding or ctime omission is used, and POSIX retains exact matching.

Only acquisition-relevant manifest fields are interpreted: package paths and the
project-level `namespace`. Unrelated DX/package settings are inert, with duplicate
JSON keys and non-JSON numeric constants still rejected. This is not full
Salesforce project-schema validation. No external `$schema`, package dependency,
login URL, script, or other setting is opened/executed. `.forceignore` rules are
not applied; this inventories available files under declared roots rather
than reproducing Salesforce deploy/retrieve selection. `.git`, `.obsidian`, and
`.obforce` directories inside packages are excluded with a warning after their
own safety checks. No directories outside the declared roots are searched.

Supported pairs are same-directory `Name.cls` and `Name.cls-meta.xml` files in
directories named exactly `classes`, anywhere below a declared package. Class
filenames use 1–40 ASCII letters/digits/underscores starting with a letter. This
validates a bounded input naming subset, not Apex syntax or deployability.
Other types/locations are excluded with `unsupported_files_excluded`. Namespace
comes only from the project manifest: absent/empty means null; otherwise it is
1–15 alphanumeric ASCII characters starting with a letter. No namespace is
inferred from filename prefixes, metadata text, package aliases, or source code.

`Selection` controls explicit namespace inclusion and optional exact class-name
filters. All supported candidates are checked for duplicates, malformed XML,
and missing pairs before filtering, so invalid or incomplete inputs cannot be
hidden by a narrower filter. Two candidate locations for the same canonical key
are a conflict, even if their bytes match or namespace selection excludes them.

## XML facts and refusal bounds

`defusedxml` is a small Python dependency introduced through Poetry for explicit
DTD, entity, and external-reference refusal. The standard library alone does not
provide those same explicit switches. See the project's
[security controls](https://github.com/tiran/defusedxml/blob/main/README.md).
Independent application bounds limit work even for documents without entities:

| Input | Refusal limit |
| --- | --- |
| Project JSON | 65,536 bytes |
| Declared packages | 128 |
| Enumerated package entries, including directories | 50,000 total |
| Relative nesting below project root | 32 segments |
| Each XML file | 65,536 bytes |
| Total supported XML bytes | 16,777,216 |
| Each `.cls` file | 1,048,576 bytes, checked by stat without opening it |
| XML elements / depth | 256 / 16, including the root |

Limits refuse the result; they never silently truncate and return complete.
Only a Salesforce metadata-namespace `ApexClass` root is accepted. DTDs/entities,
wrong roots, malformed encodings/XML, mixed content, duplicate supported fields,
attributes/nested content on supported fields, and invalid values fail with
`ModelError` (exit 2). XML parser diagnostics and input content are not included
in safe exception display strings. Operational read/change failures use exit 1;
duplicate identities/paths use conflict exit 3.

Supported facts are trimmed decimal `apiVersion` strings (`1.0`–`999.0`, a syntax
bound rather than a claim all versions exist) and status `Active` or `Deleted`.
Salesforce documents that `Inactive` is for ApexTrigger, not ApexClass; see the
[Metadata API guide](https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_meta.pdf).
Missing supported fields remain explicitly unavailable with a warning. Unknown
XML elements (including package-version information) are bounded but ignored
with `unsupported_xml_fields`; they never supply audit facts, identity overrides,
or relationships. Apex body contents are never opened, retained, embedded, hashed,
or analyzed. This increment makes no Apex syntax/static-analysis claim.

## Coverage, hashes, and limits

Inventory completeness describes only exhaustion of available selected local
scope. Empty valid packages can be complete locally. A missing source/metadata
mate omits that candidate, reports `missing_apex_pair`, and returns **partial**
inventory/exit outcome 4. A pair with missing optional supported XML facts can
still establish inventory presence; its unavailable fields remain explicit.
Unsafe, malformed, unreadable, duplicate, or over-limit inputs return no result.

Audit is independently `unavailable`, and relationships are `not_collected`, both
with `requested=false` by design. All four audit attributes remain unavailable;
local records have no Salesforce record ID. File/Git dates never substitute for
Salesforce audit dates, and source text never establishes dependency edges.

Components are ordered by canonical key and use unchanged Thread 02 hashes,
binding, availability wrappers, and provenance label `local-apex-xml-v1`.
Checkout location, package order, raw XML formatting, source body changes, and
filesystem timestamps do not change normalized hashes. Supported fact changes
do. Warnings/coverage are separate records and must travel with the inventory.
Existing selection scope hashes do not encode package manifests/paths; equal
hashes alone cannot prove comparable local scope. No local result authorizes
marking an org component absent/deleted, overwriting a note, or rebinding a source.

The DX subset is informed by Salesforce's
[project schema](https://github.com/forcedotcom/schemas/blob/main/sfdx-project.schema.json).
Runtime never downloads that schema. Local macOS results, hosted CI, native
Windows/Linux filesystem checks, and live lifecycle qualification are separate
evidence classes; see the [roadmap handoff](../dev/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md).

## Available evidence and filesystem limits

Qualification uses synthetic temporary projects/vaults and mocked Salesforce
acquisition, with independently queried synthetic org identity. Application runtime
network and process launches are denied except for the explicitly authorized
synthetic Python interruption/concurrency/collector test harnesses. Package setup
downloads are separate from application runtime. No real sf, Obsidian, credentials,
auth, metadata, vault or settings were accessed.

The local host is macOS 27.0.1 ARM64 on observed APFS, with Python 3.12.7, 3.13.15 and
3.14.7 available. Local Python 3.15, Linux and Windows are unavailable. Native
Windows junction execution is an explicit local skip; injected reparse/timestamp
checks remain mocked evidence. Case/normalization collision fixtures unsupported
by this APFS volume remain skips, not qualification. The native POSIX permission
checks concern mode denial; they do not certify ACLs or Windows private roots.

Use stable trusted private local ancestry for both the installed application and
synthetic fixtures. Setting TMPDIR/TEMP/TMP alone does not move the application
out of a changing ancestor. Full ancestor/path/descriptor/hash checks remain;
there is no automatic race retry. No support is inferred for HFS+, case-sensitive
APFS, NTFS, ReFS, ext4, network/cloud-synced/removable storage or unobserved hosts.
Existing accepted hosted ordinary-file tests retain their own evidence class;
runner labels do not establish filesystem types.

Full synthetic process-death, concurrency, recovery and cleanup tests cover
cooperating writers and observed checkpoints. They do not establish power-loss
durability, hostile-editor exclusion, forged/coarse timestamp detection, Windows
directory fsync, atomic snapshots or atomic multi-file transactions. Windows sf
execution remains refused; #18 is outside this task. Native Obsidian preview was
optional and unavailable in Thread 14 and was not invoked here.

## Reproducing synthetic measurements

`dev/qualify_scale.py` is a developer measurement harness, excluded from packages;
it adds no public Obforce command or stable Python API. First build/install the
candidate normally into an independent environment outside the checkout. Prepare
one stable external measurement parent and a separate empty cwd. Set all three
temporary-root variables to an existing dedicated directory under that parent.
For example, on POSIX with placeholder absolute paths:

```sh
TMPDIR="/absolute/Qualification/temp" TEMP="/absolute/Qualification/temp" TMP="/absolute/Qualification/temp" PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 "/absolute/Qualification/venv/bin/python" "/absolute/obforce/dev/qualify_scale.py" --classes 1000 --edges 10000 --seed 15 > "/absolute/Qualification/scale.jsonl"
```

Run from the separate empty cwd, with the installed application under the stable
measurement ancestry. The script itself blocks socket/process audit events; it
never invokes sf. Do not run other validation that changes observed ancestry
while measuring. The JSON lines record exact Python/dependency/OS/architecture,
fixture topology, stage seconds, allocation metrics, typed planning outcomes,
counts and output digest. Preserve failed results and stderr as well as successes.
Review host-specific filesystem observations separately. No installed tooling,
org, service latency or HTTP request performance is measured.

The 1,000-class fixture uses 10,000 explicit seeded directed edges and independent
partial synthetic coverage. It cannot fit the **128 changed-file** publication
ceiling: notes plus dashboard/state would total 1,002 files. Actual 127-note and
1,000-note public builds separately verify write-free refusal; no split-batch
workaround exists. A separate 32-class/320-edge plan measures valid planning,
and a separate 12-note lifecycle qualifies publication. These independent fixtures
are not chunks of the large batch.

Stage peak **traced Python allocation** bytes include retained inputs; incremental
peak subtracts traced allocations at stage entry. Neither is total RSS. Where the
standard `resource` module is available, whole-process `ru_maxrss` is reported
separately, in bytes on macOS and KiB on Linux, including setup and tracer overhead.
It is a process high-water observation, not per-stage RSS. Tracing and host load
change elapsed times. Measurements are not throughput/service-level guarantees.

Live inventory/audit mock counts expose batched behavior. Relationship collection
retains its fixed per-ID outgoing/incoming probes, bounded to 101 total queries
including org identity, and reports partial coverage even for clean empty replies.
It cannot collect all 10,000 explicit synthetic edges for 1,000 selected classes.
No query/timeout/bound is raised and no additional live query form is introduced.

## Bounded CI test execution

Large fixture values must stay in test values/fixtures. The three original byte
payloads became pytest IDs and exceeded Windows' 32767-character environment
value limit when pytest set `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST`. Setup and teardown both failed;
those test bodies did not execute. Repeated IDs also produced enormous logs.
Explicit short IDs now identify those cases, with their complete payloads intact.
A shared test hook describes long automatic string/byte parameters by length;
collection refuses any remaining node ID above 512 UTF-8 bytes without printing
the offending identifier. This also covers explicitly supplied IDs.

CI runs the developer-only `dev/run_pytest.py` supervisor from the test-suite root.
For local reproduction, select fresh absolute log paths outside the checkout:

```sh
poetry run python dev/run_pytest.py --collect-only --log /absolute/isolated/collection.log
poetry run python dev/run_pytest.py --log /absolute/isolated/pytest.log
```

The supervisor retains combined stdout/stderr in an exclusively created log and
prefixes console lines to prevent child text becoming Actions workflow commands.
Its finite budgets are separate from all application safety limits:

| CI boundary | Budget / behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Automatic string/byte parameter description | Values over 96 bytes use length-based IDs; values remain intact |
| Collected test node ID | 512 UTF-8 bytes; collection error before test setup |
| Raw capture and emitted child console output | Each at most 2 MiB, plus a small fixed controller status |
| Child diagnostic line | 4096 bytes; overflow fails instead of printing the line |
| Collection wall time / Actions step | 5 / 6 minutes |
| Coverage suite wall time / Actions step | 45 / 50 minutes |
| Independent artifact install step / entire matrix job | 30 / 90 minutes |
| Failure diagnostics | Short tracebacks, no captured-output dumps, stop after five failure reports |
| Matrix / superseded runs | Fail fast; superseded runs in the same workflow/ref group cancel |

Output overflow, deadline or uncertain cleanup exits unsuccessfully and marks
the retained log as an incomplete bounded prefix. It cannot establish a complete
test or coverage pass. Existing log paths are never overwritten; there is no
automatic retry. A failed pytest exit remains failed. Cancellation and unexecuted
tests remain qualification gaps. Default pytest diagnostics are bounded in
`pyproject.toml`; the supervisor supplies the capture/time boundaries in CI.

The controller terminates its owned POSIX process group or uses Windows' native
`taskkill` for its owned pytest tree, then reaps the child. The outer Actions
deadlines backstop unconfirmed cleanup. This is ordinary CI process management,
not hostile-process containment or Windows sf execution. Owned-Python-tree cleanup is now observed in the accepted hosted Windows cells;
escaped/hostile descendants remain outside that evidence. The exact hosted matrix
is accepted as recorded below. No
application limit, filesystem guard, schema, payload, dependency or scope changed.
The supplied raw failure log stays private and unmodified; public tracking holds
only reviewed synthetic summaries and evidence boundaries.

The approved internal optimization snapshots note paths immutably for one batch.
Renderer and graph validation remain lazy at their original call sites, retaining

Exact note bytes, hashes, graph/move invalidation and malformed/unrelated path
refusals are compared in regressions. No renderer/schema version, input payload,

Profiling has instrumentation overhead. An interrupted partial baseline is not
a passing test, complete timing baseline or proof of the Windows timeout cause.
The detailed record retains it and the shared-coverage/installer-ancestry setup

Use `Profile.runcall(pytest.main, ...)` with explicit propagation of pytest's exit

# Fictional offline first build

This journey uses the repository's fictional Apex sample and no Salesforce CLI,
authentication, network, Obsidian process or plugins. Public Thread 12 commands
are accepted and complete, including maintainer confirmation of character
readability and four-space generated nesting. See the
[acceptance record](../dev/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md#thread-12-acceptance-and-closure--23-october-2026).
Thread 13 adds [refresh](REFRESH.md) for evidence-bearing managed vaults.
Use an installed development package (`poetry install --with dev` from the checkout)
and Python 3.12+. Package/dependency installation is separate from offline runtime.

Choose a **new absolute workspace outside this repository**, any source checkout,
existing vault, template root or application installation. Substitute the two
absolute paths below. The selected workspace parent must already exist; this
setup refuses to replace an existing workspace. Python's `shutil` copies only
the supplied fictional sample, never real metadata.

```sh
python -c "import shutil,sys; from pathlib import Path; root=Path(sys.argv[1]); root.mkdir(); shutil.copytree(Path(sys.argv[2])/'examples/sample_sfdx', root/'Fictional Project')" "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace" "/absolute/path/obforce-checkout"

obforce init --config "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace/obforce.toml" --source "./Fictional Project" --vault "./Knowledge" --workspace-id fictional --dry-run
obforce init --config "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace/obforce.toml" --source "./Fictional Project" --vault "./Knowledge" --workspace-id fictional
obforce build --config "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace/obforce.toml" --dry-run
obforce build --config "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace/obforce.toml"
```

`python -m obforce` accepts the same options as `obforce`; both are noninteractive.
A relative `--config` uses your current working directory. On Windows, quote
native paths with spaces, for example `--config "..\Fictional Workspace\obforce.toml"`;
unrooted forward-slash paths work too. Use a fully absolute path when selecting a
drive; `C:obforce.toml` and `\obforce.toml` are ambiguous and refused.
The absolute config path works from any directory. Source/vault paths inside it
resolve from its parent. Preview commands create no config, vault, state, lock,
journal, log, cache or staging artifacts. Init creates only a new config, with
an existing parent. Ordinary Python bytecode caching can be disabled separately
with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`; reads may affect filesystem access times.

The final command creates two readable ApexClass notes under
`Knowledge/Custom Code/Apex Classes`, the protected native
`Knowledge/Dashboards/Apex Classes.base`, plus `.obforce/state.json` and the
persistent writer lock. It reports local inventory complete, audit unavailable/unrequested,
and relationships not collected/unrequested, with exit 0. No Salesforce audit
dates, authoritative dependency edges or technical-debt assessment are invented.
You can open the notes yourself; Obforce does not launch or configure Obsidian.
User prose/properties, including every `technical_debt*` field, belong to you.

After adding human context or moving a note uniquely within the vault, preview
and refresh through the same explicit config:

```sh
obforce sync --config "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace/obforce.toml" --dry-run
obforce sync --config "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace/obforce.toml"
```

With unchanged source/graph/templates, these operations preserve exact note and
state bytes/mtimes, including human-only edits. New builds save private normalized
refresh evidence inside `.obforce/state.json`; legacy vaults without it refuse
refresh rather than guessing old facts. No source/Obsidian settings are changed.


Build is **initial-only**. Repeating it returns conflict 3 without altering the
vault. Any existing destination entry, including unrelated notes, `.obsidian` or
managed history, refuses. Do not delete control files to bypass this check.
Use a new explicitly selected destination for another fictional first build;
Use `sync` to refresh this newly created managed vault.

Recovery needs only the explicit config and local evidence:

```sh
obforce recover --config "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace/obforce.toml"
# Select only the operation matching the validated journal phase:
obforce recover --config "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace/obforce.toml" --rollback
obforce recover --config "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace/obforce.toml" --cleanup
```

The default is validated read-only preview. `--dry-run` is equivalent.
Rollback refuses committed evidence; cleanup refuses precommit evidence. Without
pending evidence, recovery is a write-free no-op. An edit or incomplete/unsafe
journal refuses and preserves evidence for manual resolution. Setup interrupted
before a journal can leave directories whose ownership cannot be reconstructed;
no automatic recursive removal or build retry adopts them. A successful rollback
retains the control/lock, so it does not turn the old destination into a new build.


## Exit codes

| Exit Code | Description                                            |
|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| 0         | complete selected operation/no-op                      |
| 1         | operational failure                                    |
| 2         | invalid usage/config/input                             |
| 3         | conflict/recovery required                             |
| 4         | completed operation with requested incomplete coverage |

Requested partial inventory can produce a bounded
partial first build with 4; it does not prove missing components. Precedence is
3, 2, 1, 4, 0. See [configuration](CONFIGURATION.md#public-initialization-and-initial-build-thread-12)
and [setup/recovery limits](SYNC_SAFETY.md#public-initial-setup-and-recovery-thread-12).


## Additional Information

Windows sf execution, native ACL/durability, power-loss and hostile-race guarantees
are not established by this offline example or hosted synthetic tests.


## Optional native table

Open `Knowledge/Dashboards/Apex Classes.base` yourself if native Bases is available
in your Obsidian installation. Obforce opens no app and changes no settings. The

# Refresh an existing managed vault

Thread 13 adds public `sync` for an explicitly configured managed vault created
with private refresh evidence. Examples here are fictional. See the
[quickstart](QUICKSTART.md) for a new offline build; real Salesforce operations
still require separate authorization. Internal Python interfaces are not stable APIs.

Thread 13 is accepted at correction `b43ed64` / merge `3f5e909`; #13 is closed.
Exact-merge run `40346586335`, attempt 1, passed all 12 Linux/macOS/Windows ×
Python 3.12–3.15 cells and 24 independent installs. See the
[acceptance record](../dev/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md#thread-13-acceptance-and-closure--26-october-2026)
for counts, retained failures and native/live limits. No live org or Windows sf
execution is qualified by these synthetic results.

```sh
obforce sync --config "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace/obforce.toml" --dry-run
obforce sync --config "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace/obforce.toml"
# Equivalent module entry point:
python -m obforce sync --config "/absolute/path/Fictional Workspace/obforce.toml"
```

All commands are noninteractive. `--config` is required, invocation-relative or
absolute; its source/vault/template paths remain config-relative. Native explicit
paths with spaces are supported. There is no config/home/vault/auth/default-org/
executable discovery. No source-mode/workspace/org rebinding, adoption or force mode.
Build remains initial-only, absent/empty-only and refuses repeats. Sync does not
create a missing vault or reconstruct state. Pending recovery evidence blocks sync.

## What refresh changes

Refresh applies only validated generated-property and generated-region patches.
User prose, supported YAML/comments, tags, aliases and every `technical_debt*`
property remain user-owned. Technical debt is never inferred. Creation templates
apply only to newly discovered components; an existing note is never regenerated
through a creation template. Invalid creation overrides are irrelevant when there
are no new notes. Generated overrides can invalidate existing generated output.

A uniquely moved managed note keeps its UUID and source key. Both incoming and
outgoing links use the reconciled paths, including affected neighbors whose own
source facts did not change. Duplicate IDs, vanished notes, ambiguous ownership,
unsafe paths/collisions, edited generated properties or exact generated bytes
block the entire batch. A hash match never bypasses those ownership checks.

New notes can be added. No component note is deleted automatically. A component
absent from local/partial/incomplete input retains its exact prior normalized facts
and lifecycle. Relationship refresh retains unconfirmed prior evidence as stale,
with original provenance/coverage. Offline input does not infer dependencies.
Requested live relationships remain partial/unavailable even after clean empty
responses; inventory completeness does not imply relationship completeness.

## Private state and recovery

New builds publish private state-document schema 2 at `.obforce/state.json`, with
embedded evidence schema 1: exact tracked normalized component facts, the accepted
refreshed directed graph and optional declared live inventory scope. NoteState's
schema 1, UUIDs, note/marker schemas, accepted hashes and renderer version 3 remain.
No external program is needed to retain facts between independent CLI runs.

The state is private, unencrypted local data. It can include canonical org/record
IDs and optional previously collected audit display names needed by source hashes.
No Apex body, raw CLI response, credentials, extra source paths or human note
content is added to evidence. Disabling audit-name collection does not guarantee
erasure of names in absent retained records or private recovery before-images.
Do not upload state, generated vaults or recovery material to public tracking.

Evidence is limited to 8 MiB inside the existing 16 MiB state ceiling. All other
state/JSON/graph/render/planner/writer limits apply independently, including 10,000
tracked components, 20,000 edges/40,000 observations and the 128-changed-file/32 MiB
before-plus-after transaction ceiling. Earlier bounds can refuse a smaller batch;
there is no truncation, automatic evidence eviction or partial publication.

Notes and complete state/evidence publish through the same recoverable transaction,
with state last. Full pathname/historical descriptor/birthtime/hash/absence/parent
guards, the continuous owning-handle writer lock, same-filesystem staging and
before-images remain. Journal schema 2 is unchanged. Recovery validates each
state version explicitly; schema-1 journals remain unsupported retained evidence.
There is no atomic filesystem snapshot, atomic multi-file replacement, hostile
editor exclusion or power-loss guarantee. Windows sf execution remains refused.

```sh
obforce recover --config ./obforce.toml
# Select only the operation matching validated evidence:
obforce recover --config ./obforce.toml --rollback
obforce recover --config ./obforce.toml --cleanup
```

Preview is read-only. Precommit rollback restores notes plus the complete prior
state/evidence; committed recovery cleans only proven transaction-owned material.
Intervening edits and ambiguous/incomplete evidence refuse, retaining manual-
resolution evidence. Old schema-2 journals containing legacy state still have
their version-specific recovery path; this does not migrate that vault.

Legacy state-document schema 1 lacks lossless prior facts/graph evidence. Sync,
including dry-run, refuses it with conflict 3 before acquisition. Missing, unknown,
corrupt or contradictory state/evidence also refuses. Existing notes and recovery
remain intact. There is no automatic upgrade, bootstrap or adoption. A separate
new empty destination can be built, without automatic transfer of old human
content or a claim that old UUID continuity was preserved.

## Live inventory scope and missing components

Live build/sync retain the accepted explicit live-only `--org` override and require
absolute `--sf-executable` and existing neutral `--sf-directory` paths. The adapter
independently verifies actual org identity against saved state before inventory.
Tests use mocks; these examples do not authorize real operations.

```sh
# Planned target/executable placeholders: substitute only after live authorization.
obforce build --config ./live.toml --sf-executable /fictional/bin/sf --sf-directory /fictional/neutral --inventory-scope-id fictional-reader-v1
obforce sync --config ./live.toml --sf-executable /fictional/bin/sf --sf-directory /fictional/neutral --inventory-scope-id fictional-reader-v1 --attest-comparable-inventory --dry-run
```

The optional build-time scope ID is a logical label of 1–128 ASCII letters,
digits, underscores or hyphens, not an account name or permission fingerprint.
It becomes an immutable reference bound to saved org/Selection and actual inventory
method/API version. A build without it stores no scope reference and can still
refresh safely with absence preservation. Sync cannot add/change that declaration;
no scope-rebaseline operation is implemented. Offline rejects both scope options.

On each sync that should evaluate absence, supply the matching explicit scope ID
and `--attest-comparable-inventory`. This asserts that accessible inventory scope
remained comparable from the declared build through all retained observations,
including intervening partial scans. It is your attestation, not automatic
permission verification. No principal/permission/auth query is added. Alias,
verified org ID, token equality and query success alone do not prove continuity.

Marking missing additionally requires the supported live inventory method,
unchanged Selection/method/API-version, complete exhausted/no-limit/no-warning
inventory and independently verified matching org. A complete attested empty scan
can mark all tracked notes missing while retaining them. Missing means not observed
in the selected accessible scope, not proven deletion. Positive same-source current
observation can reactivate a previously missing note without absence attestation.

Without comparability, absent lifecycle/facts/stale edges are preserved; a completed
live refresh with absent tracked keys returns at least 4 and reports unavailable
missing evaluation. Partial/unavailable scans also preserve absences. Required
acquisition failure returns operational 1 without publishing a candidate. Changed/
ambiguous source/org/workspace/Selection or declared scope/method/API reference
blocks the complete batch with 3; malformed options use 2. Scope attestation never
turns platform relationships into complete coverage.

## Preview, no-op and outcomes

Dry-run validates the complete candidate in memory and creates no config, vault,
state, lock, journal, log, cache or staging artifact. No-op preserves exact note
and state bytes/mtimes, even after human-only edits or with differently formatted
valid state JSON. Ordinary reads can affect access times. An authorized live
preview can cause sf's own auth/config/cache side effects as documented in
[the transport contract](SF_CLI.md); Obforce previews create no artifacts.

First stale/coverage/path changes can legitimately update generated content or
state; repeating unchanged observations stabilizes. No timestamp or persistent
attestation flag is written just to record a check. A valid no-op can return 4
for requested incomplete coverage. Exit precedence remains **3, 2, 1, 4, 0**:
conflict/recovery, invalid input, operational failure, completed incomplete result,
complete/no-op. Reports expose bounded categories/counts/coverage, not private facts.

See the [roadmap handoff](../dev/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) for actual local/hosted
results, remaining platform limits and acceptance status. Enhancement #18 remains
unimplemented; the dashboard extension is described below.


## Dashboard refresh (Thread 14)

Sync now includes a protected [native Apex Classes dashboard](DASHBOARDS.md).
Valid Thread 13 evidence-bearing vaults add it only when the destination is
absent; no existing file is adopted. Notes and corresponding state retain their
accepted source/graph/ownership contracts. Dashboard edits, missing/moved files,
ambiguity or collisions block the whole batch. Its exact saved baseline uses an
optional dashboard-schema-1 record inside state-document schema 2, while evidence
schema 1, NoteState schema 1 and journal schema 2 remain. MTF-2 advances only the
renderer fingerprint to version 4 for available UTC audit date projections.
Dashboard changes share publication, rollback, committed cleanup and no-op/preview
guards with notes/state. Older executables refuse the extension; use this version
for these vaults and recovery. Legacy evidence-less sync still refuses.

The MTF-2 table update replaces only a clean exact saved dashboard baseline.
Existing human debt/status/severity/review fields are never renamed or backfilled;
new-note Boolean/blank defaults do not authorize whole-note recreation. Human
Boolean decisions remain preserved. New reserved
`sf_created`/`sf_last_modified` dates patch only after both generated baselines
validate. Edited generated dates block the entire batch like all reserved fields.

## Direction, endpoints and provenance

`MetadataComponent*` is the **referencing source**; `RefMetadataComponent*` is the
**referenced target**. One normalized `Edge` supplies both `references(key)` and
`referenced_by(key)`. A → B therefore affects A's outgoing and B's incoming view.
Self-edges and both directions of cycles are retained without recursive traversal.
These are platform-reported references, never proof of runtime behavior or
comprehensive impact analysis.

Each private endpoint retains type, namespace, name and record ID, including null
values. Resolution requires an exact supported ApexClass ID/type/name/namespace
match against the supplied selected live inventory. Apex IDs normalize from
validated 15-character or checksum-verified 18-character form to 18 characters;
queries use only canonical 18-character IDs. Empty reported namespace normalizes
to null. Namespace/case distinctions remain significant. No name-only match,
namespace inference, default org or cross-source mapping is attempted.

Unmatched supported endpoints are `external`; missing identity/type/name data
remains `unresolved`; other component types are `unsupported`; contradictory
known-ID/name/namespace descriptors are `identity_mismatch`. All stay explicit
private descriptors. This includes unsupported **referencing** endpoints in
incoming views, such as a fictional Flow → ApexClass observation. No additional
component record/note is generated. A resolved key identifies an inventory
component, not ownership of a note; later rendering may link only through an
explicit validated managed-note mapping. There is no note discovery or adoption.

Exact directed pairs are deduplicated. Each retains a sorted set of distinct
method/coverage/stale observations, including separate outgoing/incoming probe
provenance. Contradictory descriptors remain separate edges; contradictory
coverage remains separate evidence. Response ordering, duplicates, raw attributes,
incidental endpoints and collection times do not change semantic hashes. Raw
records, warning text, stderr, selectors and URLs are not retained in graph
results or diagnostics. Endpoint descriptors and canonical payloads are private
metadata and must not be logged or copied into public reports.

The graph-specific endpoint/evidence records support unresolved sources without
changing frozen `ComponentKey`, `Relationship`, component/scope hashes, ownership
or note/state schemas. The existing Relationship record continues to represent
resolved-source evidence. Thread 09 separately supplies strict state serialization/validation
and old/new managed path mappings; it never replaces stale relationship evidence.

## Fixed collection and independently verified identity

The caller supplies the explicit executable, neutral existing working directory,
explicit target and a normalized `LiveInventory`. It must separately obtain
live authorization for that target and those operations. The adapter reissues
Thread 05's exact `SELECT Id FROM Organization LIMIT 2` and requires consistent
complete identity evidence plus the same verified org/workspace binding as the
inventory. Incompatible prior source/selection is refused before queries.
Retargeting an alias cannot rebind the graph. Separate calls still require stable
trusted CLI/auth configuration and accessible metadata scope; they are not an
atomic metadata/auth snapshot.

For each selected, validated Apex ID, in sorted ID order, issue exactly one
outgoing and one incoming Tooling query. The fixed eight-field projection is:

```sql
SELECT MetadataComponentId, MetadataComponentName,
       MetadataComponentNamespace, MetadataComponentType,
       RefMetadataComponentId, RefMetadataComponentName,
       RefMetadataComponentNamespace, RefMetadataComponentType
FROM MetadataComponentDependency
WHERE MetadataComponentId = '<validated 18-character Apex ID>'
  AND MetadataComponentType = 'ApexClass'
```

Actual queries are single-line; incoming probes use `RefMetadataComponentId` and
`RefMetadataComponentType` in the same equality structure. Unselected opposite
endpoints are retained as external/unsupported descriptors. An anchor outside
the query's fixed ID/type filter is a conflict. A conflicting anchor name or
namespace remains unresolved evidence with explicit contradiction coverage.
Missing projected keys, unexpected fields or malformed values cause typed
validation refusal. Reported null remains distinct from a missing key.

No body, symbol table, unrelated User/customer data, name filter, keyset/range,
IN, COUNT, ORDER BY, OFFSET, arbitrary endpoint, continuation, Bulk API, query file
or alternative transport is used. The accepted [CLI boundary](SF_CLI.md) retains
its executable/target/working-directory controls, JSON/byte/time gates, cleanup,
redaction and Windows refusal. `_Session` now accepts internal budget overrides;
Thread 05 defaults and offline acquisition behavior remain unchanged.

| Application boundary | Maximum |
| --- | --- |
| Queries, including identity | 101 total; at most 100 relationship probes |
| CLI replies per selected ID/direction | 1; no supported continuation strategy |
| Returned relationship rows before deduplication | 10,000 total |
| Stdout per query | 1,048,576 bytes |
| Stderr per query | 65,536 bytes |
| Collection wall budget | 300 seconds |
| Per-process wall budget | Lesser of 60 seconds and remaining collection budget |
| Endpoint descriptor text | 512 characters per field; an application bound |
| In-memory graph | 20,000 directed pairs, 40,000 supplied observations |

Budgets are internal, finite and not exposed tuning options. A record-budget
exceeding reply contributes safe page evidence but no accepted edges from that
reply. At the documented 2,000-row query cap, coverage records possible truncation;
the cap is never an exhaustion certificate. Query/time exhaustion stops further
calls; failures count against the query budget. Graph overflow refuses rather
than dropping prior evidence. CLI internal auto-fetch and column requests mean
CLI invocation counts are not exact HTTP request counts. Process creation and
cleanup retain the limits documented in SF_CLI.md.

## Coverage and stale refresh

Inventory, audit and relationship coverage remain independent. This optional
adapter returns a new coverage record without changing the supplied inventory,
audit coverage or component facts/hashes. Offline relationships remain
`not_collected`, `requested=false`, with no call to this adapter.

**Release limitation:** The current fixed read-only allowlist cannot independently
prove MetadataComponentDependency exhaustion, complete type support or permission
visibility. Every usable probe, including consistent empty results, yields
`partial` requested relationship coverage. No usable probe or no selected endpoint
yields `unavailable`. Both produce outcome 4 under the existing coverage contract.
There is no caller switch that can make platform collection complete. Actual
request API version stays unknown, rather than inferred from class compilation
ApiVersion or the reviewed documentation version.

Count/done/continuation/warning/stderr/extra-result-field contradictions are
retained as safe `PageEvidence` booleans/counts and fixed warning codes; later
clean replies cannot clear them. A continuation is never executed. Optional
process/envelope failures become `query_unavailable`; the redacted boundary does
not distinguish permission, unsupported object/field, authentication, timeout or
cleanup failure. Required identity failures remain operational/coverage errors.
Validation/config/conflict errors propagate with unchanged precedence
**3, 2, 1, 4, 0**. No fallback broadens access.

`refresh_graph` accepts only validated in-memory snapshots with exactly matching
binding and Selection. Partial, failed, unsupported or uncollected refreshes
retain prior non-reaffirmed evidence as stale with original provenance/coverage.
Exact current evidence reaffirms a previous observation; changed evidence coexists
with the old stale observation. Prior resolved identities are retained on stale
edges even when absent from a later inventory; this is historical evidence, not
proof of current presence, absence or deletion. Explicit note paths still govern
link eligibility. Repeated identical failures do not grow evidence indefinitely.
A complete **synthetic** snapshot can test authoritative empty replacement; the
platform collector never generates such completeness. No state file is loaded,
reconstructed, adopted or written.

Each note fingerprint includes incident outgoing/incoming evidence, graph-wide
coverage, matching source/scope and relevant supplied note paths. It composes the
unchanged legacy graph helper with graph-specific descriptors (including unresolved
sources). Moving either managed endpoint invalidates the neighbor's graph hash;
unrelated path moves do not. No component source hash changes. Coverage changes
can invalidate all notes that need to display the changed collection limitation.
Fingerprints provide invalidation evidence, not permission to overwrite notes.

# Internal Apex candidate rendering

Thread 13 [public refresh](REFRESH.md) uses this renderer only for generated
candidates on existing notes, followed by exact baseline-preserving patches.
Persisted private graph/fact evidence supplies historical inputs; renderer version
3, four-space generated nesting and all existing fingerprint/escaping contracts
remain. Creation templates still apply only to new notes; human prose/YAML is
never regenerated or reindented.

Thread 07 implements deterministic **candidate** rendering in
`renderer/templates.py` and `renderer/notes.py`. This is an internal interface,
not a stable public Python API. Thread 12 connects it to public initial build. The renderer reads no existing note and performs no patching,
adoption or publication. Thread 09 separately adds internal read-only
[state/move reconciliation](SYNC_SAFETY.md); Thread 10 adds internal read-only
planning; accepted Thread 11 publication/recovery and Thread 12 public orchestration
compose these existing primitives.
A complete new-note candidate must never be applied to an existing note.
Thread 08 separately supplies
[bounded in-memory preservation](NOTE_FORMAT.md#internal-existing-note-parsing-and-preservation-thread-08)
for caller-supplied bytes and saved baselines.

## Inputs, identity and output

The caller supplies an accepted normalized ApexClass component, independent
Coverage, a matching DependencyGraph, explicit managed-note paths, normalized
layout/privacy options and a persistent canonical lowercase UUID. The renderer
does not invent/regenerate identity, inspect a vault, load state, acquire source,
invoke Salesforce/Obsidian, or discover authentication. Supplied bindings,
selection, namespace options and relationship coverage must agree. Offline
graphs must remain empty and relationships explicitly `not_collected`.

`note_paths` proposes new portable paths under the configured Apex directory:
`DemoService.md` or `fictional_package/DemoService.md`. These proposals do not
establish existing-note ownership. Names retain case/Unicode/namespace; unsafe
segments fail rather than being silently renamed. Explicit managed paths may
represent moved notes, but only the caller's previously validated mapping can
establish that fact. The renderer does not verify filesystem ownership.

Paths require `.md`, at most 1,024 characters, 32 segments, and 240 UTF-8 bytes per
segment, in addition to the shared portable/reserved-name rules. Wikilink control
characters (`#[]^%&;` plus backticks, `!` and braces) are refused. Full paths and
all shared directory spellings are compared under NFC plus casefold; file/parent
collisions are refused too. Two different namespace spellings cannot silently
share a portable directory. No destination is inspected or created.

`render_generated` returns only the marker-interior string, exact reserved
property values and source/graph/render/region hashes. `render_new_note` additionally
returns a complete new-note string, explicit path and a separate creation hash.
Candidate strings have UTF-8/LF semantics and one terminal newline. The engine
serializes sorted, quoted property keys and JSON-encoded scalar/list values,
a valid flat YAML subset. Quoted keys also preserve names such as `null`/`false`.
There are no YAML tags, aliases, nested mappings or duplicate keys. This thread
needs no runtime YAML parser dependency; it does not parse existing frontmatter.

The engine owns UUID/schema, the frozen `sf_*` allowlist, and exactly one ordered
marker pair on separate lines. Templates cannot supply frontmatter or markers.
Unknown `sf_*` names and attempts to supply reserved creation defaults fail.
Optional creation defaults are explicit flat user properties; all remain
user-owned after creation. Defaults are `type: salesforce_component`,
`tags: [salesforce]`, Boolean `technical_debt: false` (MTF-2), blank strings
`tech_debt_severity`/`tech_debt_status`, and `last_reviewed: null`.
Only Boolean debt overrides are accepted for new notes; other supported custom
human values remain distinct. Boolean human decisions remain preserved during
patching; metadata never assesses technical debt. The maintainer authorized false
throughout fictional/example/test defaults without historical unassessed data.
Creation requires
Business Context, Known Issues / Technical Debt, and Additional Information
exactly once. Generated sections require Salesforce Metadata, Coverage,
References and Referenced By exactly once.

Unavailable, absent and observed-null audits are omitted from properties and
explained separately in the generated body. Audit-name omission removes available
names from both output contexts and properties. No body, org ID, record ID,
internal endpoint, raw response or incidental collection timestamp is projected
into output. Metadata strings use the bounded inline escaping contract below;
property strings use YAML-compatible JSON quoting. Internal wikilinks use
only separately validated explicit paths and escaped display labels. Explicit
user creation defaults are authored content, not source metadata or inferred facts.

## Installed assets and explicit overrides

The two known names are:

- `apex_generated.md.j2`: generated-section presentation.
- `apex_created.md.j2`: initial human body after the generated region.

`load_template(name, directory)` checks only that known filename in an explicit
absolute override root. A missing root/file falls back **per template** to
`importlib.resources.files('obforce')` packaged assets. Existing invalid overrides,
unsafe roots/files and read failures do not fall back. There is no cwd search,
metadata-based template discovery, Jinja filesystem loader, recursive scanning,
include, import or inheritance. Other files in the root are never discovered.

Save overrides as UTF-8 with LF line endings on every platform. Carriage returns
(including CRLF), other unsupported control characters and reserved structure are
refused without normalization or fallback. For a Python-created override, use
`path.write_text(text, encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')`; checkout attributes do not
control line endings of files created at runtime.

Root ancestors and known files are checked with lstat; links/reparse points,
special files and multiply linked template files are refused. Bounded reads
compare pathname/descriptor identity, size and mtime and recheck parents. POSIX
no-follow/nonblocking open flags are used where available. These are read-side
checks requiring a stable trusted local override tree, not hostile filesystem
race isolation or later publication qualification. Config paths already resolved
by the loader cannot reveal links that were resolved before rendering.

Overrides are user-selected local code-like input. The sandbox alone does not
prevent CPU/memory exhaustion. This implementation therefore accepts a finite
**interpolation-only Jinja subset**: literal Markdown and exactly one
`{{ name | section }}` for each engine-produced generated section. The available
names are `metadata`, `coverage`, `references`, `referenced_by`. The `section`
filter accepts only serialized engine strings. Reorder sections and add ordinary
presentation text; retain their required headings. Creation templates are literal
human-section Markdown with no context slots. Supply flat creation property
defaults through the explicit caller argument, never template YAML.

For example, this fictional generated override retains every required slot:

```jinja
{{ metadata | section }}

{{ references | section }}

{{ referenced_by | section }}

{{ coverage | section }}
```

StrictUndefined remains enabled. Globals/tests/default filters are cleared;
Python attributes and callables are denied. AST validation refuses loops,
conditionals, calls, arithmetic, attributes, indexing, constants/expressions,
macros, imports/includes, filters other than `section`, missing/duplicate slots
and unknown names. There are no model/Path objects, IDs, arbitrary dicts,
filesystem/process/network helpers or side effects in template contexts.
Errors are typed and redacted, without template/source contents or local paths.

| Refusal bound | Maximum |
| --- | --- |
| Each UTF-8 template | 16,384 bytes |
| Each template AST | 256 nodes |
| Each normalized input string | 4,096 characters |
| Aggregate primitive input per candidate | 2 MiB / 100,000 nodes |
| Supplied components or managed paths | 10,000 |
| Incident directed edges | 2,000 |
| Creation properties | 128 total, including reserved/default keys |
| Aggregate section context / each rendered section | 512 KiB |
| Complete new-note candidate | 1 MiB |

Bounds refuse, never truncate. Finite interpolation precludes template-controlled
loops, recursion, expression amplification and unbounded iterator execution;
output size is checked before candidate acceptance. This is not an OS CPU/memory
isolation facility. Read errors are OperationalError; invalid templates/structure
are ConfigError; invalid normalized inputs are ModelError; identity/scope/path
ambiguity is ConflictError. Existing error/exit precedence is unchanged.

## Relationships and invalidation

References and Referenced By derive from the same accepted directed graph.
Supported exact resolved endpoints become links only with explicit validated
managed paths. Unmapped, unsupported, external, unresolved and identity-mismatch
endpoints stay labeled text; no extra component notes are created. Self-edges,

are retained without recursion. Endpoint IDs are never display labels.

Inventory, audit and relationship coverage are displayed independently with
method, requested status, pagination, limits, API version and warnings. Each edge
also retains its original method/coverage/staleness. These are platform-reported
references, not runtime proof or comprehensive impact analysis. The accepted
collector cannot establish exhaustion: requested platform relationships remain

Source hashes and all existing hash helper contracts remain unchanged. The

It does not change the accepted graph fingerprint or component source hash.

Exact generated-template bytes, graph/path and relevant coverage changes affect

# Internal Salesforce CLI process boundary

Thread 04 implements `sources/sf_cli.py`, an internal transport boundary with
mocked protocol tests and fictional Python child-process tests. It adds no
public CLI command or live source adapter. It does not verify an org, collect
Apex inventory/audit fields, normalize records, or decide collection coverage.
Thread 05 now supplies a separate internal [live Apex adapter](LIVE_SOURCE.md)
that verifies org identity and interprets bounded inventory/audit coverage.
The transport itself remains unchanged. Internal interfaces are not a stable Python API.
No Salesforce CLI installation or authentication is needed for tests/help/version.

Thread 04 is accepted and delivered at merge `6980b26`. Exact-commit
[run 39314787749](https://github.com/jeffshurtliff/obforce/actions/runs/39314787749)
passed all 12 Linux/macOS/Windows Python 3.12–3.15 cells: Linux/macOS each
executed 340 tests; Windows each reported 329 passed and 11 expected skips.
Every cell passed standalone checks, fresh build/Twine and both independent
artifact installations. The Windows skips include the nine POSIX collector
cases, POSIX wrapper-symlink case and existing FIFO case. These results qualify
those tests/refusals, not real CLI or Windows sf execution. Future native Windows
support is tracked in [#18](https://github.com/jeffshurtliff/obforce/issues/18),
an unstarted enhancement outside v0.1.0 that does not block Thread 05.

## Execution contract and platform boundary

A caller must separately obtain authorization for the selected live org and
operations. Constructing a request or loading a live config grants none.
`run_sf` takes one explicit absolute `Path` to a trusted CLI installation and one
existing absolute working directory. There is no executable discovery, PATH
search, default org, arbitrary command string, extra flag list, shell, stdin,
query file, output file, or plugin/auth/deploy/Apex-execution operation.

The allowlist is exactly:

| Internal operation | Arguments following the executable |
| --- | --- |
| `VERSION` | `version --json` |
| `QUERY` | `data query --json --target-org <target> --query <SELECT text>` |
| `TOOLING_QUERY` | Same query arguments, followed by `--use-tooling-api` |

Targets must be explicit, nonempty, trimmed, at most 256 characters, without
control characters or leading `-`. Spaces and shell metacharacters stay in one
argument. Queries are complete internal-caller SELECT statements, at most
16,384 characters; controls, comments, and semicolon-separated statements are
refused. This is a conservative transport gate, not a SOQL grammar validator.
Future callers must use reviewed field/query templates and validated values;
this module never interpolates user values into SOQL. No Thread 05 query
selection or org-identity logic is implemented here.

Only **POSIX direct execution** is implemented. The supplied path resolves to an
executable regular file; symlinked installations resolve to their target. Trust
in the chosen installation, its interpreter, plugins and filesystem remains the
caller's responsibility. This is not executable authenticity verification or
protection against a hostile installation/path replacement.

`.cmd`, `.bat`, `.ps1`, and `.com` command wrappers are refused, including wrappers
hidden behind symlinks. **All Windows execution, including native `.exe` paths,
fails closed** pending a safe native launcher and bounded descendant-cleanup
implementation. No wrapper parsing, inferred sibling Node launcher, `cmd /c`,
PowerShell, or `shell=True` fallback is available. Mocked Windows refusal tests
are not native qualification. Other platforms also fail closed.

The caller selects a neutral working directory outside source/vault/template
roots; it is validated but never created. No Obforce files are written. The
child receives only inherited `HOME`/`TMPDIR`, fixed language/CLI controls and
`PATH=os.defpath`. Arbitrary `SF_*`/`SFDX_*` overrides, tokens, proxies,
`NODE_OPTIONS`, Python hooks and inherited PATH entries are not forwarded.
Home is passed to let a future authorized CLI reuse its own existing auth;
Obforce never opens auth stores or `.env`. A shebang using `env node` therefore
requires a trusted Node on that standard path; other installation layouts may
fail operationally and have not been qualified. No runtime/CLI installation or
update is performed. Fixed controls disable telemetry/auto-update/update checks,
set fatal CLI logging and cap CLI query auto-fetch at 10,000 records. These are
controls for a trusted CLI, not isolation from its plugins. The CLI may itself
read/write auth/config/log/cache state or refresh authentication during future
authorized read queries. Read-only Salesforce operations do not imply a
third-party filesystem or network sandbox.

## Collection and refusal limits

| Boundary | Hard maximum |
| --- | --- |
| Process wall deadline | 60 seconds |
| Stdout | 8,388,608 bytes |
| Stderr | 65,536 bytes |
| JSON container depth | 32 |
| Accepted JSON value nodes | 100,000 |
| Returned records | 10,000 |
| Cleanup wait | 2 seconds |

Callers can reduce time/byte limits; zero, nonfinite, boolean, negative and
above-ceiling values fail. POSIX binary pipes are nonblocking and multiplexed.
Each read requests at most remaining allowance plus one overflow sentinel byte;
stdout accumulation never exceeds its allowance, and stderr is counted and
discarded. Overflow terminates the request before text decoding or JSON parsing.
There is no `communicate()` buffer, background reader thread, spool file, or
truncation-as-success behavior. The deadline covers both pipe draining and
leader exit, including closed pipes and descendants holding pipes open.
OS process creation itself cannot be forcibly interrupted by this Python gate.

A fresh process session/group is killed and the direct child reaped on success,
failure, overflow, timeout, or interruption. Pipes and selector descriptors close.
Failure to confirm cleanup is an operational error. Cooperative descendants in
the same group are covered, even after the leader exits; hostile descendants
that escape the group and OS-uninterruptible processes are outside this trusted
local executable boundary. No general process-containment guarantee is claimed.

## JSON and privacy

UTF-8 output must contain exactly one bounded JSON object. Duplicate keys,
nonfinite numbers, excessive nesting/nodes, invalid JSON/encoding, missing known
fields and wrong known-field types fail. Depth is scanned before decoding JSON;
node counts are checked on the byte-bounded parsed object. Warning texts, error
messages, stack traces, raw stdout/stderr, selectors and paths are never included
in errors or logging. No logging is performed. Errors suppress raw exception
chains and use fixed `ConfigError` (exit 2) or `OperationalError` (exit 1)
diagnostics; a CLI exit/status never becomes an Obforce exit code directly.
Two line-specific Bandit annotations cover the intentional subprocess import
and shell-free call after explicit executable/argv validation; no global rule is
disabled.

Query success requires exit 0 plus integer `status: 0`, an object `result`, an array of object
`records`, a nonnegative integer `totalSize` at least the returned count, and a
boolean `done`. `records` is an array of objects. An output-file result is
unsupported. Optional `nextRecordsUrl` must be a bounded nonempty string and is
retained as private data, never followed. Warnings accept the framework's string
or structured-object forms but expose only presence. Compatible extra query
properties remain private for a later adapter to interpret; they are not trusted
normalized facts. Version success uses the bare oclif object and retains only
`cliVersion`, `architecture`, and `nodeVersion` strings. Nonzero query errors
validate `name`, `message`, and positive integer `status`; version errors use an
`error` object with `name`/`message`. Malformed errors fail safely too.

The reply's data/continuation fields are excluded from its repr. They remain
private: callers must not serialize/log the reply or use raw fields in notes.
Stderr exposes only presence. A successful exit with an error envelope fails;
a failure exit with a success envelope also fails. Empty stdout never succeeds.

`done`, `totalSize`, returned records, continuation, and warning/stderr presence
are observations. Even `done: true` with fewer records than `totalSize`, or with
a continuation signal, remains visible to the later adapter. No success/empty
result proves complete inventory, verified org identity, accessible comparable
scope, or audit/dependency completeness. See [coverage](COVERAGE.md) and
[configuration/error precedence](CONFIGURATION.md). Coverage errors and normalized
identity remain the later adapter's responsibility.

## Official contracts reviewed on 19 October 2026

Reviewed via documentation/source reads, without executing `sf`:

- [Salesforce data query reference](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_data_query.html)
  documents query, explicit target, JSON and Tooling flags. Obforce deliberately
  omits file/output/bulk/deleted-row options and never relies on CLI default orgs.
- [Salesforce JSON support](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/sfdx-setup/guide/sfdx-dev-cli-json-support.html)
  explains command schemas and additive JSON evolution.
- Official [query implementation](https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-data/blob/a0cdb671f42af74e31a782c34c5cdcc22e1ea5b0/src/commands/data/query.ts)
  uses auto-fetch with a configurable limit and warns about missing records;
  [result schema](https://github.com/salesforcecli/plugin-data/blob/a0cdb671f42af74e31a782c34c5cdcc22e1ea5b0/schemas/data-query.json)
  requires records, totalSize and done. The schema is for the inner result.
- [SfCommand serialization](https://github.com/salesforcecli/sf-plugins-core/blob/efe58eff7bf546045e6beca16856104ffcc7eca9/src/sfCommand.ts)
  wraps query success in status/result/warnings.
- [oclif version](https://github.com/oclif/plugin-version/blob/fb2f672e93879a94bb3365f6d5f878715a53a2ae/src/commands/version.ts)
  returns three fields without verbose mode;
  [oclif core](https://github.com/oclif/core/blob/b5c0aefa2c68c921a5c85eadd12fce097ddc33d1/src/command.ts)
  serializes that result directly and failures under `error`.
- [Python subprocess security](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/subprocess.html#security-considerations)
  warns that Windows batch files may invoke a system shell even with `shell=False`.
  This is the reason for wrapper refusal, not a reason to enable a shell.

These are observed official contracts, not a tested installed CLI/version pin.
No real CLI or platform support claim follows from source inspection. Refresh
contracts and obtain targeted authorization before any future live validation.

Thread 12 public live initial build requires explicit `--config`, optional live-only
`--org` override, and both absolute `--sf-executable`/`--sf-directory` options.
The directory must be existing and neutral; no PATH/default-org/auth discovery is
added. The accepted adapters verify actual org identity before graph/planning.
Implementation and lifecycle tests use mocked process replies only. Recovery
never calls this transport. Live previews may cause sf's own local state changes
as described above; Obforce previews create no artifacts. Windows execution
remains refused and enhancement #18 remains outside v0.1.0 and NOT STARTED.

# Internal state, reconciliation, planning and transactions

## Pre-implementation contract — 20 October 2026

This internal increment accepts explicit caller-supplied vault/state paths and
normalized binding/selection inputs. It never discovers cwd/home/auth/config,
invokes source transports, adopts notes, or writes state. Public commands,
batch planning/reporting, publication, locks, journals and recovery remain later
threads. Only synthetic vaults are authorized for validation.

The accepted immutable `NoteState`, SHA-256 and source/graph/render/creation hash
contracts remain unchanged. `SavedNote` pairs a NoteState with immutable exact
saved marker-interior bytes. These bytes come from the prior accepted candidate
or patch, never from the current note to reconstruct ownership. They include
original LF/CRLF bytes. Compare both strict generated-property values and exact
region bytes before accepting a discovered note; verify the saved bytes against
the saved exact-byte SHA-256 too. Hashes are integrity aids, not authentication.
Never save user prose or user-owned properties as generated baselines. Creation
fingerprints remain creation-only and are not persisted as render hashes.

## Version-one private wire document

UTF-8 JSON without BOM, duplicate keys, nonfinite/floating numbers or coercion.
Every object has an exact key set; unknown versions/keys/types refuse. Serialization
uses existing compact canonical JSON (sorted object keys, literal Unicode), notes
sorted by canonical component key, canonical sorted selection/warnings, and one
terminal LF. Arrays of field strings retain order. No timestamps, host paths,
aliases, credentials, raw source/transport records or human regions are persisted.

Root keys: `state_schema` (integer 1), `binding`, `selection`, `scope_hash`,
`coverage`, `notes`. Binding is exactly workspace_id/mode/org_id; local requires

## Discovery and reconciliation

The explicit existing absolute vault is the discovery root. The explicit expected
state path must be exactly vault/.obforce/state.json; only this document is read
separately. Exclude `.git`, `.obsidian`, `.obforce` directory segments under NFC
plus casefold; their contents are opaque. Validate boundary entries but do not
traverse them. Other directories are scanned completely; ordinary non-Markdown
files are stat-checked but not read. Markdown suffix matching is case-insensitive.
Read all Markdown within finite bounds. Conservative managed indicators are
case-insensitive `obforce` or any `sf_` occurrence in raw Markdown, including
malformed identity/marker/frontmatter content. Indicators require successful
Thread 08 parsing and exact tracked identity/baselines; false positives refuse
for review instead of silently ignoring a potentially damaged managed note.
Ordinary notes without indicators stay unadopted, untouched and unrecorded.

Missing state is allowed only with explicit `initial=True`, no managed indicators,
and no supplied existing document. This means an empty **managed** initial scope;
unrelated files may exist but none is adopted. Empty bytes are corrupt, not an
empty document. A valid empty notes array similarly cannot coexist with managed
notes. Missing/corrupt/unknown state never reconstructs ownership.

Reconcile only a unique canonical UUID with its exact validated source key/schema.
A unique in-vault move changes only candidate NoteState.path; UUID/key/content,
all baselines and prior hashes remain unchanged. Return immutable deterministic
paths and explicit old/new path changes for later incoming/outgoing graph/render
invalidation; do not calculate a batch plan or rehash/rewrite notes. Duplicate or
copied IDs, multiple notes per component, identity edits, vanished tracked notes,
untracked managed notes, old-path unowned collisions and ambiguous paths refuse.

Caller binding and selection must exactly match saved evidence; changed scope or
workspace/local/live/org rebinding refuses. Collection outcomes can differ from
scope. No source inventory absence is evaluated here: a vanished note is a
conflict, whereas a component absent from offline/partial/unavailable/changed

relationships. Stale evidence and independent coverage remain intact.

## Read assumptions and refusal limits

Reject traversal/escape, nonabsolute roots, source/template/repository overlap
against explicit caller-supplied excluded roots, unsafe symlink/junction/reparse
ancestors/entries, special files and multiply linked regular files. Reject
portable case/NFC spelling collisions, reserved names and file/parent collisions,
including unrelated entries in the scanned tree. Managed paths also retain

must supply every source/template/application root, not infer them from cwd.

Reads use lstat plus descriptor identity/size/mtime/ctime/link/mode checks,
no-follow/nonblocking flags where available, bounded reads, parent snapshots and
final whole-scan rechecks. Cross-API Windows pathname/descriptor comparisons use
explicit integer `st_birthtime_ns` for creation time alongside device/inode,
mode/link-count/size/mtime; unavailable birthtime refuses. Windows `st_ctime_ns`
can mean creation for lstat and metadata change for fstat, so those two values
are not compared to each other. Full ctime remains in repeated path observations
and descriptor-before/after checks; descriptor birthtime and safety are rechecked
after reading too. POSIX retains its full ctime comparison. See the official
[Python stat timestamp contract](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/os.html#os.stat_result.st_birthtime_ns),

[descriptor timestamp source](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.7/Python/fileutils.c#L1037-L1041)
and [upstream issue 157671](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157671).

and partial iteration refuse. Permission/I/O errors are redacted OperationalError
(1); unsafe/corrupt state, note/path/source conflicts are ConflictError (3);
invalid explicit caller inputs are ModelError (2). Existing exit precedence
3, 2, 1, 4, 0 remains unchanged. Display no raw JSON/YAML/content/path diagnostics.

## Thread 11 pre-implementation transaction contract — 20 October 2026

This records the historical internal design before dependent implementation.
